content.english: "And the serpent was cunning" (ve-ha-naḥash haya ʿarum). It is plausible¹ that this serpent was one [individual] of the serpent-kind² — that it had four [legs] and that there was in it [discursive] understanding³…
content.comments: ¹ yaqrubu (يقرب) — "it is plausible"; Ali's marker for a tentative reading he is prepared to defend without staking his strongest claim on it. ² jins (جنس) — "natural kind, species"; the Aristotelian-derived term, standard in Karaite grammar and kalām. ³ maʿrifa (معرفة) — "[discursive] understanding, [direct] recognition"; in kalām, the cognitive grasp of a particular, often distinguished from ʿilm (propositional knowledge).

content.hebrew: וכׄבתׄ. וכאן מכלפא בכׄלאף בקיה̈ גׄנסה ולדׄלך אורדה בהא אלתעריף לימיזה מנהא בהדׄא אלמעני ולתוגׄה אלדׄם אליה עלי מא פעלה כאן דׄלך דאלא עלי קבחה וכונה מכרוהא [מ]נה
content.english: …and malice¹. And it was [made] morally accountable², in contrast to the rest of its kind, and for that reason [the verse] brought in upon it the definite article³ to single it out from them in this respect, and so that censure might be directed against it on account of what it did — this [feature of the verse] indicating its ugliness and its being disapproved [by Him].
content.comments: ¹ khabīth (خبيث) — "evil-natured, malign"; here paired with the gloss of ʿarum as moral cunning. ² mukallaf (مكلَّف) — "subject to taklīf, [religiously] accountable"; the agent upon whom obligation rests. ³ alif lām al-taʿrīf (ال التعريف) — "the definite article"; standard Arabic-grammar term for Hebrew הָ-/Arabic الـ. The argument: the article in ha-naḥash singles out this serpent as the particular accountable agent.

content.hebrew: קולה מכל חית השדה – בעד קול מן קאל אנה מלאך
content.english: His saying "more than any beast of the field" (mi-kol ḥayyat ha-sadeh). [This is] after the statement of one who said that it [the serpent] was an angel.

content.hebrew: Gen 3:5
content.english: Gen 3:5

content.hebrew: ונפקחו עיניכם – ליס יריד בה טׄאהרה בל מא אורדה בעדה מן תפסירה והו והייתם כאלהים (בראשית ג:ה) יעני תצירון מתׄל אלמלאיכה̈ אלמכׄתצה̈ [במ]עארף ליסת מעכמא ודׄלך תכׄרץ מנה ותמויה ולעלה אסתכׄרגׄ דׄלך מן לקב אלשגׄרה̈ בעץ דעת טוב ורע
content.english: "And your eyes shall be opened" (ve-nifqeḥu ʿeyneikhem). He [the serpent] does not intend by it its surface sense, but rather what he brought after it as its interpretation¹ — namely, vi-hyitem k-Elohim 'and you shall be as gods' (Gen 3:5), meaning, 'you will become like the angels, who have a special purchase on cognitions² that you do not [yet] possess.' And this [statement of his] is a fabrication³ on his part and a dissimulation⁴; and perhaps he extracted [this pretext] from the designation of the tree as ʿeṣ daʿat tov va-raʿ 'the tree of the knowledge of good and evil'.
content.comments: ¹ tafsīr (تفسير) — "interpretation, gloss"; the explanatory paraphrase a speaker himself supplies for his preceding utterance. ² maʿārif (معارف, pl. of maʿrifa) — "items of [restricted] cognition"; here, the knowledge proper to the angels alone. ³ takharruṣ (تخرُّص) — "baseless fabrication, [speculative] guesswork"; Qurʾānic and kalām term for an assertion made without warrant. ⁴ tamwīh (تمويه) — "dissimulation, [the] gilding-over [of falsehood]"; rhetorical term for misleading speech that disguises its true purport.

content.hebrew: Gen 3:7
content.english: Gen 3:7

content.hebrew: ותפקחנה – קולה וידעו כי עירמים הם (בראשית ג:ז) – תקדיר מענאה עלמא למא כאנא עריאנאן נפור נפס אחדהמא מן משאהדה̈ אלאכׄר לה בהדׄה אלצורה̈ אדׄ לא יגׄוז כונהמא כאמלי אלעקל והמא עריאנאן פלא יעלמאן כונהמא כדׄלך. פוגׄב ל[דׄל]ך אלע[ד]ל ען טׄאהרה ו[תא]וילה [ע]לי [הדׄ]א אלחד. ו[א]לדׄי תגׄדד עלמהמא בה הו נפור אחדהמא ען רויה̈ אל[אכׄ]ר [ע]ריאנא ואכׄתשאה מן נטׄרה בהדׄה אלחאל בעד [כונה]מא בכׄלאף דׄלך כק׳ ויהיו שניהם ערמים האד[ם ואש]תו ולא יתבוששו (בראשית ב:כה) ולם יקל ולא ידעו ליכון
content.english: "And [their eyes] were opened" (va-tippaqaḥna). His words va-yedʿu ki ʿeyrumim hem 'and they knew that they were naked' (Gen 3:7) — the supplied reading¹ of its meaning is: 'they came to cognize, [in their being naked,] an aversion in the soul of one of them at the sight of the other in this state'. For it is not admissible that the two of them, possessing perfection of intellect, should have been naked without knowing themselves to be so. So it was necessary, on that account, to depart from its surface reading and to interpret² it on this construal. What newly came to their cognizance, then, was the aversion of one of them to the sight of the other naked and his shame at the sight of him in this state — [a state] which contrasted with what was before, as in the verse va-yihyu sheneihem ʿarummim ha-ada[m ve-ish]to ve-lo yitboshashu 'and the two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed' (Gen 2:25); and he did not say ve-lo yadʿu 'they did not know it' — so that…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taqdīr. ² taʾwīl (تأويل) — "interpretation, esoteric reading"; in Karaite usage, the principled departure from the surface reading (al-ẓāhir) when reason or other verses require it.

content.hebrew: עכסא מן וידעו כי [עירמ]ים [הם] (בראשית ג:ז) פאלי ה[דׄא...............] אנה אשאר בקולה דעת טוב ורע (בראשית ג:כב) לא מא יקאל מן ...... אלמאכולאת ומצׄארהא וגיר דׄלך אדׄ לם ידׄכר אנהמא א.......
content.english: …the converse of va-yedʿu ki [ʿeyru]mim [hem] (Gen 3:7). And to this [point] […] he was alluding by his words daʿat tov va-raʿ (Gen 3:22) — not to what is said about […] foodstuffs and their harms and the like, since he did not mention that the two of them […]…

content.hebrew: ענד אכל תׄמר עץ הדעת מערפה̈ דׄ[ל]ך [ב]ל [ק]אל ותפקחנ[ה] עיני שניהם וידעו כי ערמים הם (בראשית ג:ז). פאן פסר טוב ורע (בראשית ג:ה) מא יסתחסן מן סתרה̈ אלעורה̈ ויסתקבחה מן כשפהא באלעאדה̈ מן טריק אלא[ד]ב פהו ראגׄע אלי מא תקדם דׄכרה מן נפור נפס אלמר ען משאהדה̈ גירה לה מהתוכא ושהותה רויתה מסתורא וליס אכל הדׄה אלתׄמרה̈ מוגׄבא לפעל אלשהוה̈ ואלנפור אלמדׄכורין פיהמא ואנמא הו תעאלי פעלה פיהמא באלעאדה̈ ענד אכלהמא להא כמא יפעלה מן אלצחה̈ ואלסקם פי אלעבד ענד מא אכל מכצוצה̈
content.english: …[acquired] at the eating of the fruit of the tree of knowledge a cognizance of that. Rather, he said va-tippaqaḥna ʿeynei sheneihem va-yedʿu ki ʿerummim hem 'and the eyes of the two of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked' (Gen 3:7). So if one interprets tov va-raʿ (Gen 3:5) [as referring to] what is held proper in the covering of the privates and what is held improper in their exposure — by way of social propriety¹ — then this reduces to what was already mentioned: the aversion in the soul of the man at the sight of another exposed before him, and his desire for the sight of him covered. And the eating of this fruit is not what brought about the operation of the said appetite and aversion within them. Rather, He (may He be exalted) performed this in the two of them by way of the customary order² at the moment of their eating of it — just as He performs health and illness in [His] servant at the moment of his eating specific [foods]…
content.comments: ¹ adab (أدب) — "social propriety, [cultivated] refinement"; the body of cultivated norms of decorum, distinguished from strict religious obligation. ² al-ʿāda (العادة) — "the [established] custom"; in kalām, the regular order of natural processes that God maintains continuously.

content.hebrew: ומערפה̈ מנאפע אלמאאכל ומצׄארהא תסתפאד באלתגׄרבה̈ או באלסמע. פאמא אן יפעל פי אלעאקל לא ען טריק פבעיד. ולא ימת[נע] כון תׄמר עץ הדעת גׄאריא מגׄרי בעץׄ אלמאאכל אלדׄי ענד אכלה באלעאד[ה̈ גׄ]על אלקדים עז וגׄל פיה אלדׄכא וצחה̈ אלתמייז וכאן אכלה מפסדה̈ פנהאה[מ]א [ע]נה.
content.english: …and the cognizance of the benefits of foodstuffs and their harms is acquired by experience¹ or by hearsay-instruction². As for its [coming about] in a rational agent through no [intelligible] route — that is far-fetched³. And nothing prevents the fruit of the tree of knowledge from functioning as some foodstuffs [do] — those in which, at the moment of their consumption, by way of the customary order, the Eternal (mighty and majestic) installs sharpness of intellect⁴ and soundness of discrimination⁵; and yet [in this case] its consumption was [also] corrupting, and so he prohibited the two of them from it.
content.comments: ¹ tajriba (تجربة) — "experience, [empirical] trial"; standard kalām epistemic category. ² samʿ (سمع) — "hearsay, [transmitted] instruction"; in kalām, knowledge acquired through authoritative report — contrasted with ʿaql (reason) and tajriba. ³ baʿīd (بعيد) — "far-fetched, improbable"; Ali's marker for a strained reading. ⁴ dhakāʾ (ذكاء) — "sharpness of intellect, mental keenness." ⁵ ṣiḥḥat al-tamyīz (صحة التمييز) — "soundness of discrimination"; the reliability of the cognitive faculty in drawing distinctions.

content.hebrew: Gen 3:11
content.english: Gen 3:11

content.hebrew: מי הגיד לך כי ערום את[ה] – תקדיר מעאנה מן אכׄ[בר]ך אני א[כר]ה משאהדתך עריאנא או מן ערפך אלנפור ען אן אר[אך] עריאנא או גיר הדׄין אלתאוילין ממא יטאבק דליל אלעקל פי אנהמא לא יגׄוז [אן יכו[נא] עריאנין ולא יעלמאן דׄלך מן אנפסהמא מע כמאל עקלהמא ותכ[ליפ]המא ה.
content.english: "Who told you that you were naked?" (mi higgid lekha ki ʿarom at[a]). The supplied reading of its meaning is: 'who told you that I find the sight of you naked detestable?', or 'who made known to you the aversion to your being seen by Me naked?', or some interpretation other than these two, [provided it is] of a kind that conforms to the demonstration of reason — namely, that it is not admissible that the two of them should have been naked and not have known it of themselves, given the perfection of their intellect and their being morally accountable.

content.hebrew: Gen 3:22
content.english: Gen 3:22

content.hebrew: [ויאמר י]י אלהים [הן האדם הי]ה כאחד ממנו – קיל [.......כואח]ד מנה יעני כואחד מן אולאדה אלמכׄארגי׳ן מנה פי באב...........ואלגם באחואל דניא[ה] ואלאגׄתהאד פי מערפה̈ מא ינפעה [ומא] יצׄרה מנהא [וקב]ל דׄל[ך] כאן מסתריחא מן מ[תׄ]ל הדׄה אלאמור ויגׄוז אן יקאל צאר כואחד מנא יעני מן אלמלאיכה̈ פי באב אלמערפה̈ במא יצׄרה וינפעה. אי קד קוי דׄהנה וגׄאד תאמלה למערפה̈ דׄלך. פלא יומן מן גׄהתה אן תרך פי גן עדן אן ימד ידה אלי עץ החיים ויאכל מן תׄמרה פיחיי ללדהר טלבא [מ]א עאד בנפעה ודפע אלמצׄרה̈ ענה כק׳ ועתה פן ישלח ידו וג׳ (בראשית ג:כב) וקבל אכלה מן עץ הדעת קד כאן עלי גׄמלה̈ מן אלתמייז ואלדׄהן מעהא צח [ת]כליפה לכנה ענד אכלה מן עץ הדעת זאד צפא דׄהנה וקוה̈ דׄכאה וגׄודה̈ תאמלה וצחה̈ תמייזה
content.english: "[And the LORD] God [said: behold the man has be]come like one of us" ([va-yomer Y]Y Elohim [hen ha-adam hay]ah ke-aḥad mimmennu). Some have said: […like on]e of us means like one of his descendants who issue from him in respect of […] being distressed by the conditions of [worldly] life and the exertion of striving for the cognizance of what benefits him and what harms him among them — though before that he had been at ease from suchlike matters. And it is admissible that one say: 'he has become like one of us' means like one of the angels in respect of cognizance of what harms him and what benefits him — that is, his mind has been strengthened and his reflection has come to suffice him for the cognizance of that. So He no longer felt secure, on his side, in leaving him in the Garden of Eden, lest he stretch out his hand to ʿeṣ ha-ḥayyim and eat of its fruit and live forever, seeking what would redound to his benefit and ward off harm from him — as in the verse ve-ʿatta pen yishlaḥ yado etc. (Gen 3:22). And before his eating of ʿeṣ ha-daʿat he had already been [possessed] of a measure of discrimination, and of mind alongside it; the validity of his being made accountable was [thereby] established. But at his eating of ʿeṣ ha-daʿat his mind grew clearer, his sharpness stronger, his reflection more excellent, and his discrimination sounder.

content.hebrew: ועתה פן ישלח ידו – תקדירה נגרשנו פן נשלח ידו
content.english: "And now, lest he stretch out his hand" (ve-ʿatta pen yishlaḥ yado). Its supplied reading is negarshennu pen yishlaḥ yado 'let us drive him out, lest he stretch out his hand'.

content.hebrew: וקולה ואכל וחי לעולם – ליס אכלה מנהא מוגׄבא דואם כונה חיא בל אלקדים עז וגׄל יכׄתאר דׄלך למא יראה מן אלצלאח ול[ו אכ]ל מנהא מע כונה מכל[פ]א למא כאן יסתמר [כ]ונה חיא לא אלי גאיה̈ כאלקדים עז [ו]גׄל פי אס[תמר]אר כונה חיא למא פי דׄלך ממא יקתצׄי אלתכליף.......מן מט[י]ע תכליפה ה. מסלה̈ אדׄא כאן ח[כמה ע]ליה ענד אכלה עץ הדעת באלמות פכיף יקול אנ[ה א]ן יאכל מעץ החיים עאש אבדא אלדׄי הו במתׄאבה̈
content.english: And his saying "and he shall eat and live forever" (ve-akhal va-ḥai le-ʿolam). His eating of it [the tree of life] is not what would necessitate the perpetuity of his being alive. Rather, the Eternal (mighty and majestic) chooses that for him in view of what He sees of right action¹. And even were he to eat of it while [still] morally accountable, his being alive would not endure without limit — for it is the Eternal (mighty and majestic) [who sustains] the continuation of his life on account of what [accountability] entails of taklīf-related considerations […] from one who is obedient to his obligation. — A question²: if it had [already] been decreed against him at his eating of ʿeṣ ha-daʿat by death, how then does He say that if he eats of ʿeṣ ha-ḥayyim he would live forever — which is to the same effect [as the decree of death]…
content.comments: ¹ ṣalāḥ (الصلاح) — "right action, [moral] soundness"; in the Muʿtazilite kalām that informs much Karaite theology, the ethically right course, distinguished from al-aṣlaḥ (the optimal). ² masʾala (مسألة) — "question, dialectical problem"; the Karaite dialectical-question marker that opens a hypothetical objection answered below.

content.hebrew: קולה לא ימות.........ליס בין אלקולין תנאקץׄ לאן קולה כי ביום [אכלך] ממנו מות תמות (בראשית ב:יז) פי צׄמנ[ה] מהמא לא יאכל מעץ [החיים] לאנה קד דל עלי דׄלך בעד חכמה עליה באלמות א[דׄ]א אכל מעץ החיים באן קאל ועתה פן ישלח ידו ולקח גם מעץ החיים ואכל וחי לעולם (בראשית ג:כב) ה
content.english: His words 'he shall not die' […]. There is no contradiction between the two statements, for his words ki ve-yom [akhalkha] mimmennu mot tamut 'for on the day you eat of it, you shall surely die' (Gen 2:17) implicitly contain the proviso 'so long as he does not eat of ʿeṣ [ha-ḥayyim]' — for he has already indicated this, after the decree of death against him on his eating of ʿeṣ ha-daʿat, by saying ve-ʿatta pen yishlaḥ yado ve-laqaḥ gam mi-ʿeṣ ha-ḥayyim ve-akhal va-ḥai le-ʿolam 'And now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat and live forever' (Gen 3:22).

content.hebrew: Gen 4:7
content.english: Gen 4:7

content.hebrew: הלא אם תיטיב שאת – יעני אליס אן תבת ואחסנת פעלך גפרת לך ולפטׄ נשיאה יקע עלי אלגפראן כק׳ ומה לא תשא פשעי (איוב ז:כא) לא ישא לפשעכם (שמות כג:כא)
content.english: **"Is it not so — if you do well, [you shall be] borne up?"** (*ha-lo im tetiv seʾet*). [It] means: 'Is it not [the case] that if you repent¹ and improve your conduct² it is forgiven you?' And the word *neśiʾa* ('lifting / bearing') is applied to forgiveness³, as in [the verse] *u-meh lo tissa pishʿi* 'and why do you not bear my transgression?' (Job 7:21), [and] *lo yissa le-fishʿakhem* 'he will not bear your transgressions' (Exod 23:21).
content.comments: ¹ tubta (تبتَ) — "you repent"; the form-I verb of t-w-b, the standard kalām term for repentance. ² aḥsanta fiʿlaka (أحسنتَ فعلك) — "you improve your conduct"; the outward manifestation paired with tubta as the inward turn. ³ ghufrān (غفران) — "forgiveness, pardon"; the standard Qurʾānic/kalām term for divine remission. Ali's point is a philological one: Hebrew נשיאה (lit. 'lifting') is a recognized idiom for forgiveness, as the proof-texts demonstrate.

content.hebrew: – וקולה ואם לא תיטיב לפתח חטאת רובץ – יעני אן דׄנבך כאלמלאזם לך אלראבץׄ יקאל ואן לם תחסן עמלך אלי באב אלקבר אלכׄטא ראבץׄ עלי באב קברך אלי אן תקום יום אלבעתׄ ויתעלק בך כקולה פי אל[תגׄו]ז
content.english: And his saying **"and if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door"** (*ve-im lo tetiv la-petaḥ ḥaṭṭat roveṣ*). [It] means: that your sin is like one cleaving¹ to you, crouching². It is said: even if you do not improve your conduct [all the way] to the door of the grave, the sin is crouching at the door of your grave until you arise on the day of resurrection³, and it cleaves to you, as he says concerning *al-[tajwīz]*⁴…
content.comments: ¹ mulāzim (ملازم) — "cleaving, [unremitting] adherent"; the inseparable companion. Ali reads Hebrew רובץ ('crouching') as metaphor for the sin's tenacious adherence to the sinner. ² rābiḍ (رابض) — "crouching"; the Arabic gloss matches Hebrew רובץ exactly and is the standard rendering at this verse in the Karaite tafsīr tradition. ³ yawm al-baʿth (يوم البعث) — "day of resurrection"; the standard Karaite/kalām term for the eschatological raising of the dead. Ali extends the verse's threat past death: the sin clings to one in the grave and confronts one again at the resurrection. ⁴ The MS is broken here; the editor restores *al-[tajwīz]* but the referent is uncertain. Given the proof-text in the next segment (Job 20:11, on bones full of youth lying down in the dust), Ali is plausibly citing a verse on aging or death; the restoration is offered tentatively.

content.hebrew: במתׄל דׄלך עצמותיו מלאו עלומיו ועמו על עפר תשכב (איוב כ:יא)
content.english: In the like of that: *ʿaṣmotav malʾu ʿalumav ve-ʿimmo ʿal ʿafar tishkav* 'his bones are full of his youthful vigor, and with him it shall lie down in the dust' (Job 20:11).

content.hebrew: – וקולה ואליך תשוקתו – יעני אן קיאד א[לכׄט]א כאן בידך פי פעלה ואלאנצראף ענה לכונך קאדרא עלי דׄלך מתמ[כנא] מנה כק׳ תמשל בו (בראשית ד:ז). וקיל אן קיאד אלתובה̈ אליך וסהל עליך לקדרתך עלי דׄלך ה.
content.english: And his saying **"and to you [is] its longing"** (*ve-eleikha teshuqato*). [It] means: that the rein¹ of [si]n was in your hand for its enacting and for the turning away from it, since you have been made capable² of that and enabled³ over it, as in [the verse] *timshol bo* 'you shall rule over it' (Gen 4:7). And some have said: that the rein of repentance⁴ is [directed] to you and made easy for you, by virtue of your capacity for that. End⁵.
content.comments: ¹ qiyād (قياد) — "rein, [the strap by which one is led]"; the metaphor for control or governance over an object. ² qādir (قادر) — "capable"; the kalām attribute of the agent who has been granted the ability to act, paired with mutamakkin as the two standard preconditions for moral accountability. ³ mutamakkin (متمكِّن) — "enabled, [in firm possession of the power to act]"; the kalām complement to qādir, denoting the unobstructed possession of the ability. ⁴ al-tawba (التوبة) — "repentance"; the standard kalām term, here reread by some commentators as the implied antecedent of 'its' in 'and to you is its longing.' ⁵ Ali closes the segment with the letter ה (Hebrew hē), which functions in his manuscript as a paragraph-end marker.

content.hebrew: Gen 4:15
content.english: Gen 4:15

content.hebrew: לכן כל הורג קין – י[ע]ני לאגׄל מא חצל מנה מן אלאעתראף בכׄטאה ואלתדׄלל ואלכׄוף עלי נפסה [מן] קתלה ואן יקאד בה
content.english: **"Therefore, whoever kills Cain"** (*lakhen kol horeg Qayin*). [It] means: on account of what came forth from him [Cain] by way of confession of his sin¹, self-abasement², and fear for himself of being killed and of being retaliated against³ for it.
content.comments: ¹ iʿtirāf bi-l-khaṭaʾ (اعتراف بالخطأ) — "confession of [his] sin"; the formal kalām act of acknowledging one's offense, often paired with tadhallul as the inward preconditions for the lifting of full penalty. ² tadhallul (تذلُّل) — "self-abasement, [humble] submission"; the interior disposition that accompanies iʿtirāf. ³ an yuqāda bi-hi (أن يُقاد به) — "that he be retaliated against / led [in retribution] for it"; the technical idiom from q-w-d for lex talionis, etymologically related to qiyād ('rein').

content.hebrew: – וקולה שבעתים – יעני חצול אלאק[תצא]ץ מן קאתלה עלי אלתמאם ואלכמאל
content.english: And his saying **"sevenfold"** (*shivʿatayim*). [It] means: the obtaining of retribution¹ from his killer fully and completely.
content.comments: ¹ iq[tiṣā]ṣ (اقتصاص) — "retribution, [exaction of] just recompense"; the legal idiom from q-ṣ-ṣ standard in Karaite legal and kalām texts. The number seven is read as an idiom for completeness rather than a literal multiplier.

content.hebrew: – וקולה וישם יי לק[ין אות] לבלתי [הכות אתו כל] מו[צאו – יעני אן] ע[ז וגׄ]ל עמל מעה איה̈.......לאגׄלהא ענה מן ירום קתלה אמא בהיבה̈ גׄעל.....ל כׄלאף אלמעתאד או ימנע מן כאן יחאול קתלה באפה̈ יערץׄ לה [כמא] גׄפת יד [י]ר[ב]עם [ל]מא מדהא אלי אלנבי וקאל לאמר תפשוהו (מלכים א׳ יג:ד) ה
content.english: And his saying **"and the LORD set for C[ain a sign], so that [none who] f[ound him should strike him down]"** (*va-yasem YY le-Q[ayin ot] le-bilti [hakkot oto kol] mo[ṣʾo]*). [It] means: that the (Migh[ty and Ma]jestic) wrought for him a sign¹ […] on account of which whoever sought to kill him would be turned aside from him — either by an awe² placed […] contrary to the customary [order]³, or He would prevent whoever was attempting to kill him by a calamity⁴ that would befall him, [as] the hand of [J]er[ob]oam withered⁵ when he stretched it forth toward the prophet and said *le-emor tipshuhu* 'saying, "seize him!"' (1Kgs 13:4). End⁶.
content.comments: ¹ āya (آية) — "sign, [miraculous] mark"; the Qurʾānic/kalām term for a divinely produced sign, here the protective mark placed on Cain. ² haybah (هيبة) — "awe, [overpowering] dread"; a state instilled in the would-be killer to deter him from acting on his intent. ³ khilāf al-muʿtād (خلاف المعتاد) — "contrary to the customary [order]"; in kalām, what deviates from al-ʿāda — the regular order of natural processes God maintains continuously. The protective awe is thus framed as a miraculous suspension of the ordinary. ⁴ āfa (آفة) — "calamity, [bodily] affliction"; the harm sent upon the would-be killer as a preventive intervention. ⁵ jaffat yad (جفّت يد) — "the hand withered"; Ali alludes to 1Kgs 13:4, where Jeroboam's outstretched hand dried up when he commanded his men to seize the prophet — his prooftext that God can intervene through bodily affliction to thwart an attempted assault on a protected figure. ⁶ Ali closes again with the ה paragraph-end marker.

content.hebrew: Gen 6:3
content.english: Gen 6:3

content.hebrew: ויאמר יי לא ידון רוחי באדם – ידון קיל ינגמד רוחי קיל מראדי יעני לא ינגמד מראדי פי אלאמהאל עלי אלאדמי עלי אלאבד אי ואן א[מ]הלת עליהם מדה̈ חסב מא תקתצׄיה אלחכמה̈ פי אלתכליף פאני לא אדים אלאמהאל עלי מעאציהם אלי אלאבד
content.english: **"And the LORD said: my spirit shall not contend in man"** (*va-yomer YY lo yadon ruḥi va-adam*). [As for] *yadon* — some have said: yanjamid 'shall perdure'¹; [as for] *ruḥi* — some have said: 'my intent'². [The verse] means: my intent shall not perdure regarding the granting of reprieve³ to humanity forever — that is, even though I have granted them a reprieve for a period, in accordance with what wisdom⁴ requires in [the matter of] moral accountability⁵, I shall not perpetuate the reprieve over their disobediences forever.
content.comments: ¹ yanjamid (ينجمد) — "shall congeal, perdure, [remain fixed]"; here taken as the gloss of yadon, in the sense of 'shall continue in force.' ² murād (مراد) — "intent, [object of] will"; the kalām term for what an agent purposes. Reading ruḥi as 'my intent' spiritualizes away the anthropomorphism of God's 'spirit.' ³ imhāl (إمهال) — "granting of reprieve, [forbearance over time]"; the standard kalām term for God's delay of punishment to allow time for repentance. ⁴ al-ḥikma (الحكمة) — "[divine] wisdom"; the principle that governs God's apportionment of obligation and consequence. ⁵ al-taklīf (التكليف) — "[the laying-on of] moral obligation, accountability"; the central kalām category for God's holding humans answerable for their conduct.

content.hebrew: – וקולה בשגם הוא בשר – קיל בסבב אלדׄי קד צאר הו איצׄא מתׄל סאיר אלבשר יעני אלחיואן אלגיר נאטק אדׄ קד מאתׄלוה פי ארתכאב אלמשתהאאת אלקביחה̈
content.english: And his saying **"in that he too is flesh"** (*be-shaggam hu basar*). Some have said: 'by reason that he too has become like the rest of flesh' — meaning the non-rational animal¹ — since they have come to resemble it in the pursuit of base appetites².
content.comments: ¹ al-ḥayawān ghayr al-nāṭiq (الحيوان غير الناطق) — "the non-rational animal"; the standard philosophical designation for the beasts, taken over by the kalām and the Karaites from the Aristotelian-Avicennan tradition. ² al-mushtahayāt al-qabīḥa (المشتهيات القبيحة) — "base appetites, [morally] disgraceful objects of desire"; the kalām category of bodily desires whose pursuit is morally blameworthy.

content.hebrew: וקולה והיו ימיו מאה ועשרים שנה – יעני אגׄעל לאמהאלהם אגׄלא נהאיתה מאיה̈ ועשרין סנה̈ פאן הם אקלעוא ותאבוא ואלא אהלכתהם. וקד אבעד תפסיר ידון ינגמד מן טריק אללגה̈ מן חית אן לגה̈ דׄלך אצל[ה]א
content.english: And his saying **"and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years"** (*ve-hayu yamav meʾah ve-ʿesrim shana*). [It] means: I make for their reprieve¹ a term whose end is 120 years — if they desist² and repent³, [well and good], and if not, I shall destroy them. And [some] have deemed far-fetched⁴ the interpretation of *yadon* as *yanjamid* on philological grounds, since the lexis of that [verb] has its root[s]⁵…
content.comments: ¹ imhāl (إمهال) — "reprieve, granting of [extended] time"; see seg. 194. ² aqlaʿū (أقلعوا) — "they desist, [refrain from sin]"; the kalām term for the cessation of the sinful action — the outward complement to tāba (repent). ³ tābū (تابوا) — "they repent"; from t-w-b. ⁴ abʿada (أبعد) — "deemed far-fetched / improbable"; Ali's marker for a reading he rejects on linguistic grounds. See [[ali-genesis-project]] CONVENTIONS on baʿīd. ⁵ Mid-thought break — the discussion continues into the next segment, with a grammatical analysis of which verbal root supplies yadon.

content.hebrew: נונאן מתׄל וישב חרבו אל נדנה (דברי הימים א׳ כא:כז) בגו נ[דנה] (דניאל ז:טו) וידון פיה נון ואחד. וקיל אן תפסירה יחא[כ]ם יכׄאצם ואמרה דון בוזן מול א[ת ב]ני יש׳ (יהושע ה:ב) והו במעני ידין עמים (תהלים ז:ט) אלדׄי אמרה דין או הדן בוזן מיל או המל אלדׄין יגׄוז כון כל ואחד מנהא [אמרא כק]ולה כי אמילם (תהלים קיח: י) פלגה̈ מול ואמילם ואחדה̈ והמא מן תצריפין כמא אן לגה̈ דון ודין ואחדה̈ ומרגׄעהמא אלי תצריפין. וקיל אן תפס[יר רוחי] נבותי לאן רוח [תק]ע עלי א[לנ]בוה̈ כק׳ והיי[תי רוח שקר (מלכים א׳ כב:כב)] ותהי עליו רוח יי (שופטים ג:י) יעני לא יכׄאצם רסולי ונביי אלאד[מי אלי] אלאבד. אי לא יגׄיהם באלתהדיד ואלועיד עלי מ[ע]אציהם אבדא
content.english: …[has] two nuns, like *va-yashev ḥarbo el nadnah* 'and he returned his sword into its sheath' (1Chr 21:27), *be-go ni[dneh]* 'within its sheath' (Dan 7:15); and in *yadon* there is [only] one nun. And some have said: its interpretation is *yuḥā[ki]m* / *yukhāṣim* 'he shall adjudicate / contend,' and its imperative¹ is *don* on the measure² of *mol* in *mol e[t b]ene Yisraʾel* 'circumcise the [s]ons of Israel' (Josh 5:2); and it is in the meaning of *yadin ʿammim* 'he shall judge peoples' (Ps 7:9), whose imperative is *din* — or *hadon* on the measure of *mil* or *hamel*, [these forms of] *din*; for it is admissible that each of these be [an imperative], as in his saying *ki amilam* 'for I shall fend them off' (Ps 118:10), the lexis of *mol* and *amilam* being one, and they are from two conjugations³ — just as the lexis of *don* and *din* is one, with their reference back to two conjugations. And some have said: the interpretation of [*ruḥi*] is 'my prophecy⁴,' for *rūaḥ* is applied to prophecy, as in [the verse] *ve-hayi[ti rūaḥ sheker* 'and I shall be a lying spirit'] (1Kgs 22:22), *va-tehi ʿalav rūaḥ YY* 'and the spirit of the LORD was upon him' (Judg 3:10) — meaning: my messenger and my prophet⁵ shall not contend with hu[manity] forever; that is, he shall not come to them with threat and warning⁶ over their disobediences forever.
content.comments: ¹ amr (أمر) — "imperative"; the standard Arabic-grammar term, applied here to Hebrew morphology. ² wazn (وزن) — "measure, [morphological] pattern"; the Arabic-grammar device of expressing a word's morphological shape by analogy to a standard pattern, taken over by the Karaites for Hebrew morphology. ³ taṣrīf (تصريف) — "conjugation, [verbal] derivation"; the system of inflectional and derivational verbal forms. Ali's point: don and din, like mol and amilam, are imperatives from distinct verbal stems (geminate vs. hollow root) that nonetheless converge in surface form. ⁴ nubuwwa (نبوة) — "prophecy"; the divinely communicated office, here proposed as the referent of ruḥi. ⁵ rasūl … nabī (رسول … نبي) — "messenger … prophet"; the two standard kalām designations for the prophetic role, carrying respectively the dispatching and the announcing aspects. ⁶ al-tahdīd wa-l-waʿīd (التهديد والوعيد) — "threat and warning"; the standard kalām pair for the modes of prophetic admonition concerning future punishment, the complement of al-tabshīr wa-l-waʿd (good tidings and promise).

content.hebrew: – וקולה בשגם הוא בשר – קיל יעני אני אלאן לא אעאגׄלהם באלעקובה̈ בסבב אנהם בשר פארחמהם ואמהלהם אלי מאיה̈ ועשרין סנה̈ יכון אלרס[ול] [י]אתיהם פיהא השכם ודבר (ירמיהו ז:יז) פאן רגׄעוא פי הדׄה אלמדה̈ ואלא אהלכתהם. והדׄא אלתפסיר פי בשגם הוא בשר יגׄרי מגׄרי ויזכר כי בשר המה וג׳ (תהלים עח:לט) אלמקול בעדה והוא רחום יכפר עון וג׳ (תהלים עח:לח).
content.english: And his saying **"in that he too is flesh"** (*be-shaggam hu basar*). Some have said: it means that I for now do not hasten upon them with the penalty¹, by reason that they are flesh — so I have mercy on them and grant them a reprieve of 120 years, in which the messenger comes to them *hashkem ve-dabber* 'rising early and speaking' (Jer 7:17). If they turn back in this period [well and good], and if not, I destroy them. And this interpretation in *be-shaggam hu basar* runs the course of² *va-yizkor ki vasar hemmah* 'and he remembered that they were flesh' etc. (Ps 78:39), said after which³ is *ve-hu raḥum yekhapper ʿavon* 'and he, being compassionate, atones for iniquity' etc. (Ps 78:38).
content.comments: ¹ al-ʿuqūba (العقوبة) — "penalty, [judicial] punishment"; the kalām/legal term for the consequence imposed upon the wrongdoer. ² See glossary s.v. yajrī majrā. ³ Ali says "said after which" (al-maqūl baʿdahā), but Ps 78:38 in fact precedes 78:39 in the Psalter; this is likely either a textual slip in Ali (or his copyist) for "said before which," or a reference to the order of citation rather than the order in the Psalm. We render Ali's wording as it stands.

content.hebrew: Gen 6:6
content.english: Gen 6:6

content.hebrew: וינחם ייי – אדׄא כאן אלנדם ואלמשקה̈ לא יגׄוזאן עליה תעאלי פלא בד מן תאויל מא תצׄמנה הדׄא אלפסוק מן דׄכרהמא באן יקאל רגׄע אללה למא צנע אלאדמי פי אלארץׄ ען איתׄאר צלאחה למא ט׳הר מן טלאחה ושק דׄלך עלי נביה יעני אן כאן גרצׄה בכׄלקה בני אדם תעריצׄהם באלתכליף אלי אלמנאפע אלשביה עאגׄלא ואגׄלא פלמא עצוא אסתחקוא אן ירגׄע סבחאנה ען צלאח שאנהם אלי פסא[ד ח]אלהם.
content.english: **"And the LORD relented"** (*va-yinnaḥem YY*). Since regret¹ and distress² are not admissible upon Him (may He be exalted), there is no escape from interpreting³ what this verse contains in the way of mention of those two — [and so] one says: God turned back, on account of what humanity wrought in the earth, from preferring⁴ his welfare⁵, in view of what manifested of his wickedness⁶, and that distressed his prophet — meaning: that if His purpose in His creation of the sons of Adam was their being subjected by [moral] obligation⁷ to the [comprehensive] benefits⁸, both the proximate⁹ and the ulterior¹⁰, then when they disobeyed, they became deserving that He, praise be to Him, should turn back from [intending] the soundness of their condition to the corrup[tion of] their state.
content.comments: ¹ al-nadam (الندم) — "regret"; the inner state of wishing one had acted otherwise. Standard kalām category, excluded from God by all Karaite and Muʿtazilite theology. ² al-mashaqqa (المشقة) — "distress, [psychic] hardship"; likewise excluded from God. ³ See glossary s.v. taʾwīl. ⁴ īthār (إيثار) — "preference, [active] electing"; here, God's election of human welfare as the purpose of creation. ⁵ ṣalāḥ (صلاح) — "welfare, [moral and ontological] soundness"; the Muʿtazilite-kalām category for what conduces to the agent's good. See [[ali-genesis-project]] Gen 3:22 footnote. ⁶ ṭalāḥ (طلاح) — "wickedness, corruption"; the lexical antonym of ṣalāḥ. ⁷ See glossary s.v. taklīf. ⁸ al-manāfiʿ al-shabīhah (المنافع الشبيهة) — "the [encompassing] benefits"; the Arabic adjective is uncertain in the MS — possibly al-shamīla ("comprehensive") or a sound-similar scribal variant — but the sense is clear from the immediately following enumeration into proximate and ulterior. ⁹ ʿājil (عاجل) — "proximate, [pertaining to] this-worldly [reward and benefit]"; the kalām division of benefit by temporal locus. ¹⁰ ājil (آجل) — "ulterior, [pertaining to] the [reward of the] world-to-come"; the eschatological complement to ʿājil.

content.hebrew: וקולה ויתעצב אל לבו – קיל שק דׄלך עלי [נ]ביה נח אדׄ אלאכׄיאר ישק עליהם פסאד אלאשראר [וס]מאה לבו עלי טריק אלתשביה בקלב אלאנסאן אלדׄי הו אער[ף גׄ]ארחה ואפצׄל אעצׄאה כדׄלך אלנבי ענדה [עז] וגׄל
content.english: And his saying **"and he was grieved unto his heart"** (*va-yitʿaṣṣev el libbo*). Some have said: that distressed his prophet Noah, since the upright¹ are distressed by the corruption of the wicked². And He named him [Noah] His 'heart' by way of comparison³ to the heart of the human, which is the most knowing⁴ organ⁵ and the most excellent of his bodily parts⁶ — likewise the prophet, in His sight (mighty and majestic).
content.comments: ¹ al-akhyār (الأخيار) — "the [morally] upright, [the] best"; the kalām/Karaite designation for those who fulfill their taklīf. ² al-ashrār (الأشرار) — "the wicked"; the standard antonym of al-akhyār. ³ tashbīh (تشبيه) — "comparison, [analogical] likeness"; the Arabic-grammar/rhetorical term for similitude; in kalām, also the technical term for the doctrine of divine anthropomorphism that the Karaites (with the Muʿtazila) reject — used here in the rhetorical sense. ⁴ aʿraf (أعرف) — "most knowing"; the elative of ʿārif. The heart is the seat of cognition in classical Arabic and Karaite anthropology. ⁵ jāriḥa (جارحة) — "organ, [bodily] member"; the standard anatomical term. ⁶ aʿḍāʾ (أعضاء) — "members, [bodily] parts"; collective for the limbs and organs.

content.hebrew: ........קה̈ ולאנה חאמל סרה וחאפטׄ רסאלתה פי קלבה .......אלואו פי לבו צׄ[מ]ירא לאדם אלקריב פי אלדׄכר יעני [אלא]דמי למא ערף הדׄא אלועיד דאכׄל אלגם ואלמשקה̈ קלבה ומע [דׄא]ך פלם ירגׄע ען מעאציה מן גׄנס [4]וכעת הצר לו ויוסף למ[ע׳] ביי (דברי הימים ב׳ כח:כב).
content.english: […] and because he carries His secret¹ and preserves His message in his heart […]. The vav in *libbo* 'his heart' is a pro[no]un² referring to *adam* — the proximate [antecedent] in the [verse's] mention — meaning, the human: when humanity learned of this threat, grief and distress entered his heart, and despite that he did not turn back from his disobediences — of the kind of *u-ve-ʿet hāṣer lo va-yosef lim[ʿol] b-YY* 'and at the time of his distress, he continued to be unfaithful to the LORD' (2Chr 28:22).
content.comments: ¹ ḥāmil sirrahu (حامل سرّه) — "the carrier of His secret"; the prophet as the trustee of divine revelation. ² ḍamīr (ضمير) — "pronoun, [pronominal] referent"; the Arabic-grammar term. Ali's reading: the suffix in libbo refers grammatically not to God but to the proximate antecedent adam (the human), shifting the grief to the human side and dissolving the apparent attribution of anthropopathic grief to God.

content.hebrew: Gen 6:9
content.english: Gen 6:9

content.hebrew: אלה תולדות נוח –
content.english: **"These are the generations of Noah"** (*elleh toledot Noaḥ*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ The lemma stands in the source with no commentary following — either Ali offered no comment on this verse or the gloss is lost in transmission. The MS shows only the lemma and the introducer dash.

content.hebrew: Gen 9:3
content.english: Gen 9:3

content.hebrew: כל רמש –
content.english: **"Every creeping thing"** (*kol remes*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary in the source — Ali either offered no comment or the gloss is lost.

content.hebrew: – קולה אשר הוא חי – יכׄץ אלחי דון אלמ[י]ת לכנה בחיתׄ ידׄכא חסב מא יגׄי מן בעד
content.english: His saying **"which is alive"** (*asher hu ḥai*). It restricts¹ [the permission to] the living to the exclusion of the d[e]ad — but [only] where it has been ritually slaughtered², as is set forth in what follows.
content.comments: ¹ takhṣīṣ (تخصيص) — "restrictive specification"; the kalām/uṣūl al-fiqh term for the narrowing of a general predication by a qualifying expression. ² tadhkiya (تذكية) — "[ritual] slaughter"; from dh-k-y, the Qurʾānic/legal term for the act of slaughter that renders an animal lawful for consumption. The companion verb yudhkā ("is [properly] slaughtered") is the passive.

content.hebrew: – וקולה כירק עשב – הו תמתׄיל באלכׄצׄר ואלנבאתאת יעני כמא אן אכל הדׄה אלנבאתאת מ[ב]אח עקלא כדׄלך אבחתכם תדׄכיה̈ אלחיואן ואכלה סמעא
content.english: And his saying **"like the green of the herb"** (*ke-yereq ʿesev*). This is an analogy¹ with the vegetables and plants — meaning, just as the eating of these plants is permitted² by reason³, so I have permitted to you the slaughter of the animal and its eating by [revealed] tradition⁴.
content.comments: ¹ tamthīl (تمثيل) — "analogy, [illustrative] likening"; the rhetorical move from a clearer case to the case at issue. ² mubāḥ (مباح) — "permitted, [morally] indifferent"; the Karaite/uṣūl term for the legal category between obligation and prohibition. ³ ʿaqlan (عقلاً) — "by reason, [as] rationally [known]"; Ali's contrast with samʿan below; the Karaite/Muʿtazilite epistemological distinction between truths accessible to the unaided reason and those given only by revelation. ⁴ See glossary s.v. samʿ / ʿaql.

content.hebrew: Gen 9:4
content.english: Gen 9:4

content.hebrew: אך בשר –
content.english: **"But flesh"** (*akh basar*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary in the source; the next segment glosses akh on its own.

content.hebrew: – קולה אך הו תכׄציץ מתׄל אך אשר יאכל לכל נפש (שמות יב:טז) פכׄצץ מא פיה ד[מ]ה מן גׄמלה̈ אלחיואן באלתחרים פאקתצׄי מגׄמוע דׄלך תחרים אלשכׄץ מהמאה חיא ותחרים אלמיתה̈ אלתי דמהא באק פיהא ואטלאק מא כאן חיא תׄם ספך דמה עלי וגׄה קד ערפוה
content.english: His saying **"but"** (*akh*) is a restrictive specification¹, as in *akh asher yeʾakhel le-khol nefesh* 'except what is eaten by every soul' (Exod 12:16). So it singled out what has its bl[oo]d in it from among the totality of animals by [imposing on it the] prohibition². The aggregate of [the verse] therefore requires: the prohibition of the individual [animal] whatever it might be while alive; the prohibition of the carcass whose blood is still in it; and the permitting of what was alive, and then its blood was shed in a manner that they have come to know.
content.comments: ¹ takhṣīṣ (تخصيص) — see seg. 210. ² al-taḥrīm (التحريم) — "prohibition, [the imposition of the] forbidden status"; from ḥ-r-m.

content.hebrew: – וקולה בנפשו דמו קיל פי נפסה דמה יעני אן בקא אלנ[פס] פיה בבקא אלדם פלא יאכלוה ו[פי]ה נפסה למא
content.english: And his saying **"with its life is its blood"** (*be-nafsho damo*). Some have said: '[reading the *be-* as] *fī nafsihi damuhu* — within its s[oul] is its blood' — meaning that the continuation¹ of the s[oul] in it [the animal] is by the continuation of the blood — so they shall not eat it. And [the phrase] 'in it [is] its soul' [is given] because…
content.comments: ¹ baqāʾ (بقاء) — "continuation, [perdurance through time]"; the standard kalām term for the persistence of a substance or attribute, here naming the dependence of the animal's life upon its blood.

content.hebrew: כאן טׄאהר אשר הוא חי (בראשית ט:ג) אבאחה דׄלך פאכׄרגׄה במא דׄכרה בעדה. ואלאקרב אן א[ל]וגׄה אלדׄי ינטלק להם אכלה הו אלדׄבאחה̈ פי אלבהאים ואלטאיר ואן יגׄרי דׄלך [ע]לי אלחד אלדׄי פעלה נח פי אלבהאים ואלטאיר אלדׄין קר[ב]המא [על]ות. וליס דׄלך מן תכליפנא פיגׄב אן נערף כיפיה̈ מא כאנוא אלי[....יסת]עמלונה ה
content.english: …the apparent sense of *asher hu ḥai* 'which is alive' (Gen 9:3) [might be taken as] His permitting that [the live animal], so He excluded it [from permission] by what He mentioned afterward. And the most plausible¹ [reading] is that the manner that releases [the animal] for them to eat is [ritual] slaughter² of the beasts and the fowl, and that it should proceed on the standard³ that Noah performed in [the case of] the beasts and the fowl which he o[ff]ered up as [whole burnt] offerings (*ʿolot*). And this is not part of our [own] moral obligation⁴, so it is [not] obligatory upon us to know the precise manner that they used to […use]. End.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. al-aqrab. ² al-dhabāḥa (الذباحة) — "[ritual] slaughter"; the act-noun of dhabaḥa, the legal term for the lawful slaughter that drains the blood. ³ al-ḥadd (الحد) — "the [definite] standard / limit"; the legal/grammatical term for a precisely fixed measure or definition. ⁴ taklīf (تكليف) — "moral obligation"; standard kalām term. Ali's Karaite point: the Noahide slaughter rite is not part of *our* (i.e., post-Sinaitic Israelite) obligation, so we are not bound to know its precise ritual specifications.

content.hebrew: Gen 9:5
content.english: Gen 9:5

content.hebrew: ואך את ד[מכם] לנפשותיכם אדרוש – י[קא]ל [דמ]כם מן אנפס[כם].....יעני בה קאתל נפסה. וליס דׄלך עלי כל וגׄה לאן....אל[טׄ]למה̈ פי אנואע אלעדׄאב אלדׄי יעלם או יגלב עלי טׄנה מו[ת] פיה יחסן מנה קתל נפסה ויחמל אלאלם סאעה̈ ליסתדפע אלאלאם אלמתראכׄיה̈. וליס קתל אלאנסאן נפסה ממא א[ל]יה דאע כאלטׄלם
content.english: **"But surely your [bl]ood for your lives I shall require"** (*ve-akh et d[imkhem] le-nafshoteikhem edrosh*). It is s[ai]d: '[your bl]ood from your[selves]' […] meaning thereby the one who kills himself. But this [prohibition] is not in every respect [absolute] — for […] the [op]pression¹ in [those] kinds of torture in which one knows, or it predominates in one's [reasoned] estimation², that death is [in store] in it, [in such a case] it is well [permitted] for him to kill himself and bear the pain for an hour, in order to ward off the more extended pains. And a human's killing himself is not [reckoned] among that to which there [is] a [legitimate] calling, like [a case of] oppression…
content.comments: ¹ al-ẓulm (الظلم) — "oppression, [wrongful] injury"; the kalām category for unjust harm. ² ghalaba ʿalā ẓannihi (غلب على ظنه) — "[it] predominates in his estimation"; the uṣūl al-fiqh epistemic category of well-founded probable opinion, weaker than knowledge but sufficient to ground action.

content.hebrew: ואלכדׄב וגירהמא מן אלמעאצי אלמשתהאה̈ פיכון אלועיד מתנאולא בהדׄא אלקתי[ל] מנה פיגׄב אן יכון אלמקצוד מן קתל אלאנסאן נפסה מא כאן דאעיה̈ אליה אלשבהה̈ מתׄל קתל אלהנד אנפסהם או מן יערץׄ לה אלאלאם מן קבל אלקדים תעאלי פיקתל נפסה ראחה̈ מנהא לא[ן א]לאולי בה אלצבר וסואלה סבחאנה אמאטה̈ דׄלך פקד יגׄיבה אל[ל]ה ויחצל לה אלעוץׄ אלגׄזיל או מן יקע פי מצׄרה̈ יתוהם אן קתלה נפסה אכׄף אלמא מנהא ואלמעלום או אלמטׄנון כׄלאף דׄלך לכנה לם ינעם אלנטׄר פי אלאמאראת פכאן ירתפע ענה הדׄא אלוהם. וקיל אן אלגרץׄ בקולה ואך את דמכם לנפשותיכם אדרש (בראשית ט:ה) מא שרחה בעדה מן קולה מיד כל חיה אדרשנו ומיד האדם (בראשית ט:ה) יעני אדׄא קתלכם אלחיואן אלמסבע ומא גׄרי מגׄראה אלתמס דמכם אלדׄי לאנפסכם אי אנתצף לכם באכׄדׄ אלעוץׄ [מ]נה וכדׄלך אלחאל פי מן יקתל אכׄאה. ועלי אלתפסיר אלאו[ל י]כון תקדיר אלכלאם ומיד כל חיה (בראשית ט:ה) פאכׄתצר ואו אלעטף [מנה] כאכׄתצארהא
content.english: …and lying, and others of the desire-driven¹ disobediences. So the [punitive] threat² is taken to extend to this self-killing of his. The intent of [the prohibition of] the human's killing himself must therefore be [restricted to that which] the [evidential] doubt³ called him to — such as the self-killings of the Indians⁴; or one upon whom the Eternal (may He be exalted) brings pains, so that he kills himself for relief from them — for the better course for him is patience and asking Him (praise be to Him) to remove that, and God may answer him and abundant compensation⁵ may accrue to him; or [a case of] one who falls into harm and supposes that killing himself is lighter in pain than [the harm], when what is known or estimated is to the contrary, but he did not look well into the [evidential] indicators⁶ — otherwise this supposition would have been removed from him. And some have said: the purpose of his saying *ve-akh et dimkhem le-nafshoteikhem edrosh* 'But surely your blood for your lives I shall require' (Gen 9:5) is [given by] what He explained after it, in His saying *mi-yad kol ḥayya edrshennu u-miyad ha-adam* 'from the hand of every beast I shall require it, and from the hand of man' (Gen 9:5) — meaning: when the wild predatory animal kills you, and whatever runs its course, seek out your blood that is for your[selves] — that is, requite for yourselves [by] taking the compensation [for the loss of life] from it. And likewise is the case in [the case of] one who kills his brother. And on the first interpretation, the supplied reading⁷ of the speech is *u-miyad kol ḥayya* 'and from the hand of every beast' (Gen 9:5) — so the conjunctive vav of '[and from]' was elided, just as its elision…
content.comments: ¹ al-mushtahāh (المشتهاة) — "desired, [appetite-driven objects]"; the kalām category of acts impelled by carnal appetite. ² al-waʿīd (الوعيد) — "[punitive] threat, [the warning of] coming punishment"; the kalām counterpart to al-waʿd (promise of reward). ³ al-shubha (الشبهة) — "[evidential] doubt, [the appearance of warrant]"; the uṣūl al-fiqh category of the apparent but unsound reason that mitigates culpability. ⁴ al-Hind (الهند) — "the Indians"; an ethnographic reference to suttee or ritual self-immolation, current in medieval Arabic literature. ⁵ al-ʿiwaḍ al-jazīl (العوض الجزيل) — "abundant compensation"; the Muʿtazilite-kalām doctrine that God is obligated to compensate the patient sufferer of undeserved pain with an exceeding eschatological reward. ⁶ al-amārāt (الأمارات) — "the [evidential] indicators, [probative] signs"; the uṣūl al-fiqh category of circumstantial evidence that warrants probable opinion. ⁷ See glossary s.v. taqdīr.

content.hebrew: מן אדם שת (דברי הימים א׳ א:א).
content.english: …in [the verse] *adam, Shet* '[from] Adam, Seth' (1Chr 1:1).

content.hebrew: וקולה מיד איש אחיו – ב[גיר] ואו [אלעטף ו]שרח ומיד האדם (בראשית ט:ה) יעני מן יקתל [אכׄא]ה וצחאבה [....ד]מה אטאלבה [וא]מא קאתל גירה עלי טריק דפעה [ען נפ]סה ומאלה פדׄלך ממא קד יקרר פי אלעקל חסנה̈.
content.english: And his saying **"from the hand of every man, his brother"** (*mi-yad ish aḥiv*). [Coming] without¹ the conjunctive vav, [it is] the explication of *u-miyad ha-adam* 'and from the hand of man' (Gen 9:5) — meaning: one who kills his [bro]ther or his companion, [I shall require] his [bl]ood; I make requisition for it. As for [the case of] one who kills another by way of repelling him from his [own] life and his property, that is among what reason has fixed as praiseworthy².
content.comments: ¹ wāw al-ʿaṭf (واو العطف) — "the vav of conjunction"; the standard Arabic-grammar term for the coordinating vav, taken over for Hebrew morphology. ² yuqarrir fī l-ʿaql ḥasanatuhu (يقرّر في العقل حسنته) — "reason has fixed [it as] praiseworthy"; a Muʿtazilite-Karaite formulation of the doctrine of objective rational moral value (al-ḥasan wa-l-qabīḥ al-ʿaqliyyāni).

content.hebrew: וקולה אדרש את נפש האדם – ולם י[ק]ל אד[רש] את הדם [ח]סב קולה מן קבל ואך את דמכם לנפש׳
content.english: And his saying **"I will require the life of man"** (*edrosh et nefesh ha-adam*). And he did not [s]ay *ed[rosh] et ha-dam* 'I will require the blood,' in accordance with what he said earlier: *ve-akh et dimkhem le-nafshot[eikhem]* 'But surely your blood for your [lives]' (Gen 9:5).

content.hebrew: אדרש (בראשית ט:ה) קיל הו ביאן אלגרץׄ באלמטאלבה̈ הו לאגׄל אלנפס ואנמא דׄכר טלב אלדם אולא למא כאן בקא אלנפס פי אלגׄסד בה וקיל אנה סמא אלדם נפש כקולה כי נפש כל בשר דמו הוא (ויקרא יז:יד) וקאל כי ה[ד]ם הוא הנפש (דברים יב:כג)
content.english: [On] *edrosh* (Gen 9:5) — some have said: it is the elucidation that the purpose of the requisition is for the sake of the soul, and that the requisition of the blood was mentioned first only because the continuation of the soul in the body is by it [the blood]. And some have said: that he called the blood *nefesh*, as in his saying *ki nefesh kol basar damo hu* 'for the life of all flesh is its blood' (Lev 17:14), and he said *ki ha-[d]am hu ha-nefesh* 'for the blood is the life' (Deut 12:23).

content.hebrew: Gen 9:6
content.english: Gen 9:6

content.hebrew: שופך דם האדם –
content.english: **"He who sheds the blood of man"** (*shofekh dam ha-adam*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary in the source; the next segment glosses ba-adam damo yishshafekh.

content.hebrew: קולה באדם דמו ישפך – קיל בקו[ל] אלאדם יעני שהאדה̈ אלשהוד בקתל וקיל וחכם אלאדם יעני יחכם חאכם בקתל אי לא יגׄ[ו]ז קתלה אלא בעד אן י[תׄבת] ענד אלחאכם וגׄוב קתלה. וקיל והו אקרב כון דׄלך גׄאריא מגׄרי אלתעליל פי קתל אלמקתול לאנה קאל באדם מערפה̈ ראגׄעא אלי אלמקדם דׄכרה ולם יורדה נכרה̈ פכאן
content.english: His saying **"by man shall his blood be shed"** (*ba-adam damo yishshafekh*). Some have said: 'by the [t]estimony¹ of the man,' meaning the testimony of witnesses to the killing; and some have said: 'and [by] the ruling² of the man,' meaning that a ruler shall rule in the matter of the killing — that is, his killing is not admissible except after the necessity of his killing has been [established]³ before the ruler. And some have said — and this is the most plausible — that it runs the course of [providing] the rationale⁴ for the killing of the murderer: for he said *ba-adam* with the definite article⁵, referring back to the one previously mentioned, and did not bring it indefinitely⁶; so it would [otherwise have…]
content.comments: ¹ shahāda (شهادة) — "testimony, [judicial] witnessing"; the standard legal term. ² ḥukm (حكم) — "ruling, [authoritative judicial] judgment"; here taken as the alternative reading of Hebrew ba-adam as a substantive denoting human judicial agency. ³ thabata (ثبت) — "is established, [judicially] proven"; the standard legal term for the establishment of a fact or status before the court. ⁴ al-taʿlīl (التعليل) — "providing the rationale, [stating the] efficient cause"; the uṣūl al-fiqh term for the indication of the legal reason behind a ruling. ⁵ maʿrifa (معرفة) — "[grammatically] definite"; the Arabic-grammar term for a noun made determinate by the article, the construct, or a pronominal suffix — over against nakira (indefinite). ⁶ nakira (نكرة) — "indefinite"; the contrast to maʿrifa. Ali's grammatical argument: ba-adam takes the definite article, which forces the reference to the previously mentioned man (the murderer himself), not to a generic third party such as a witness or judge.

content.hebrew: יעוד אלי שאהד או חאכם פקאל בסבב אנה ספך דם הדׄא אלאנסאן יספך דמה. ודׄלך גׄאר מגׄרי תעלילה קתל
content.english: …[have] referred back to a witness or a ruler. [But as the article-marked phrasing forces the reference to the murderer], he said: 'by reason that he shed the blood of this human, his blood shall be shed.' And this runs the course of [providing] the rationale¹ for the killing…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taʿlīl.

content.hebrew: בעץׄ אלגׄנא[ה̈ כק]ולה ואת האיש על דבר אשר ענה (דברים כב:כד) וכקולה [ומ]תה כי עשתה נבלה ביש׳ (דברים כב:כא).
content.english: …of [some] criminals, [as in] his saying *ve-et ha-ish ʿal devar asher ʿinnah* 'and the man, on account of the matter that he violated' (Deut 22:24), and as in his saying *[u-me]ta ki ʿasta nevala be-Yisraʾel* 'and she shall die, for she has done an outrage in Israel' (Deut 22:21).

content.hebrew: וקולה כי ב[צ]לם אלהים עשה את האדם – הו תעריף אלוגׄה...אלהים...קד פצל...
content.english: And his saying **"for in the [i]mage of God He made humanity"** (*ki be-[ṣ]elem Elohim ʿasah et ha-adam*). It is the elucidation of the rationale¹ […] God […] he has [made the] distinct[ion] […]²
content.comments: ¹ taʿrīf al-wajh (تعريف الوجه) — "the elucidation of the rationale / [respect under which the ruling holds]"; a near-synonym for taʿlīl; see seg. 228. ² The MS is heavily lacunose at this segment; only scattered phrases survive.

content.hebrew: ויהי גבול הכנעני – דׄכר גבול אלכ[נעני]ֿ...ול...מן חיתׄ אן ישראל יתסלמון בלאד[ה] .....י באלחד אלגרבי והו צידון אלדׄי הו פי זאויה̈ אלגרב [אלי] גׄהה̈ צפון
content.english: **"And the boundary of the Canaanite was"** (*va-yehi gevul ha-Kenaʿani*). He mentioned the boundary of the C[anaanite] […] from [the consideration] that Israel would take possession of his lands […] [beginn]ing with the western boundary, which is Sidon, that being at the corner of the west toward the direction of the north.

content.hebrew: – וקולה בואך גררה – תקדירה עד [בואך] גררה לאן מים אבתדי אלגאיה̈ אלתי פי מצידון יקתצׄי
content.english: And his saying **"as you go toward Gerar"** (*boʾakha Gerarah*). Its supplied reading¹ is *ʿad [boʾakha] Gerarah* 'until [as you go toward] Gerar' — for [the boundary]'s starting from Sidon requires…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taqdīr.

content.hebrew: [אכׄת]צאר עד קבל גררה אלתי הי אנתהי אלגאיה̈.
content.english: …the [el]ision of *ʿad* 'until' before *Gerarah* 'Gerar,' which is the terminus of the [boundary-]line.

content.hebrew: – וקולה [ע]ד עזה – הו נהאיה̈ הדׄא אלחד אלגרבי אלי גׄהה̈ דרום.
content.english: And his saying **"[un]to Gaza"** (*[ʿa]d ʿAzzah*). This is the end of this western boundary [running] toward the direction of the south.

content.hebrew: – וקולה [ב]ואך סדומה ועמורה וג׳ – יעני ומעזה עד בא׳ [ס]דומה ועמורה והו אלחד אלשרקי.
content.english: And his saying **"[as you] go toward Sodom and Gomorrah"** etc. (*[bo]ʾakha Sedomah va-ʿAmorah*). It means: and from Gaza unto [where you c]ome to [So]dom and Gomorrah; and this is the eastern boundary.

content.hebrew: – וקולה לשע – [קי]ל אנהא זגר ואסמהא איצׄא בלע ואסמהא אלמשהור [צע]ר כק׳ ומלך בלע היא צער (בראשית יד:ב). פקד כׄרגׄ בכון [צע]ר מן ארץ ישראל לדכׄולהא פי חד אלכנעני מתׄל גזה̈ ה.
content.english: And his saying **"unto Lasha"** (*Lashaʿ*). [Some have sa]id it is *Zughar*¹, and its [other] name is also *Belaʿ*, and its well-known name is [*Ṣoʿ]ar*, as in [the verse] *u-melekh Belaʿ hi Ṣoʿar* 'and the king of Belaʿ — that is, Ṣoʿar' (Gen 14:2). So it has come out [from the verse] that [Ṣoʿ]ar is [reckoned as part] of the land of Israel, on account of its [falling] within the boundary of the Canaanite — like Gaza. End.
content.comments: ¹ Zughar (زُغَر) — the standard medieval Arabic name for biblical Zoar, the site at the southern end of the Dead Sea well known to Arab geographers.

content.hebrew: Gen 11:9
content.english: Gen 11:9

content.hebrew: על כן קרא שמה בבל – [לם] ידׄכר מן הו אלקורא ויקרב אנה ייי עז וגׄל אלמקדם דׄכרה פי [אל]פסוק אלאול וערף דׄלך לנח או גירה מן אלאוליא [פ]סמית בבל.
content.english: **"Therefore he called its name Babel"** (*ʿal ken qara shemah Bavel*). He did [not] mention who the namer is; and it is plausible¹ that it is the LORD (mighty and majestic), the one previously mentioned in the first verse, and that He made that known to Noah or to others of the saints² — [s]o it came to be called Babel.
content.comments: ¹ yaqrubu (يقرب) — "it is plausible that"; Ali's preference-marker for a tentative reading. See CONVENTIONS. ² al-awliyāʾ (الأولياء) — "the friends [of God], the saints"; the standard Qurʾānic/kalām designation for those drawn near to God, often including the prophets.

content.hebrew: – וקולה כי שם בלל [י]י שפת כל [הא]רץ – טׄאהרה אלתעליל פי תסמיתהא בבל ו[ל]יס חורפהמא
content.english: And his saying **"for there the LORD confused the language of all the [ea]rth"** (*ki sham balal [Y]Y sefat kol [ha-a]rets*). Its surface sense is the providing of the rationale¹ for the naming of it [the place] as Babel — and yet the [two letters bet of Babel and the one bet of balal] are not…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taʿlīl.

content.hebrew: [מש]תקה̈ כאלאסמא אלמשתקה̈ מן חואדתׄ יסמי בהא מתׄל [על] כן...וגׄהין...[ו]חסב מא מעני פי ויקרא את שמו נוח לאמר [הוא ינחמנו ממ]עשנו (בראשית ה:כט). וא[מ]א אן יכון אחד אלבאא[ין] פי בבל לא .....
content.english: …[de]rived [in a one-to-one correspondence], as are the names derived from events that they are named after, such as *ʿal ken*… [in] two respects … and according to the meaning in *va-yiqra et shemo Noaḥ le-emor [hu yenaḥamenu mi-ma]ʿasenu* 'and he called his name Noah, saying "this one shall comfort us from our work"' (Gen 5:29). As for one of the two *bet*s in *Babel* [being an additional letter] not […]…

content.hebrew: [ב]ה בל זאיד. ויכון אצל בבל בא ולאם פקד יתר[אדף אללאם] פי הדׄה אללגה̈ והי אלסקוט כמא יתראדף פי לג[ה̈] אלקטע [אללאם פי]ֿ ימולל (תהלים צ:ו) וכדׄלך לגה̈ אלסקוט נחו ונבל כעלה כל[נו (ישעיהו סד:ה) אלדׄי]
content.english: …[in] it: rather, [the second is] additional. So the root of *Babel* is *b* and *l*, and the *lamed* [gets] reduplicat[ed] in this verbal lexis [of perishing] — for [it is the] perishing — just as it is reduplicated in the lex[is] of cutting, [the *lamed* in] *yemolel* '[the grass] is mown' (Ps 90:6); and likewise in the lexis of falling, as in *va-naval ke-ʿaleh kul[lanu]* 'and we all withered like the leaf' (Isa 64:5), [whose]…

content.hebrew: אצלה אלבא ואללאם ואלנון פיה ללאסתקבאל ו[נח]ו בעמי[ם הוא] יתבולל (הושע ז:ח) אלדׄי אללאמאן פיה מתראדפאן ואלאכתׄר פי הדׄה [אללגה̈] בנון אצליה̈ טׄאהרה̈ ומכׄתצרה̈. אן קיל אדׄא כאן ק[ד] ק[רר] תעאלי [פי] אלעקול חסן אלתחרז מן אלמצׄרה̈ בפעל מא יעוד בגׄמ[יע] ללשמל ועדם אלתשתת ואלתבאעד וכיף אחל בהולא
content.english: …root is the *b* and the *l*, and the *n* in it is for the future tense¹; and [li]ke *be-ʿammi[m hu] yitbolal* 'among the peoples [he] mingles himself' (Hos 7:8), in which the two *lamed*s are reduplicated. And most often in this [lexis] the *n* is an original letter, [either] manifest or contracted. — If it be said²: since [He] (may He be exalted) has [es]tab[lished] in the rational intellects that it is good to guard against harm by an action that redounds to all [of one's kind], by way of [their] gathering together and the absence of dispersal and mutual distancing — how then did He inflict upon these…
content.comments: ¹ li-l-istiqbāl (للاستقبال) — "for the future [tense]"; the Arabic-grammar term for the prefix-conjugation as marker of futurity, taken over for Hebrew morphology. Ali's grammatical claim: the nun in n-b-l (root of nabal etc.) is the imperfect-prefix, not part of the root. ² See glossary s.v. in qīla / kāna al-jawāb.

content.hebrew: אלקום מא גׄרי מגׄרי אלעקובה̈ עלי מ[א] פעלוה מן בנא אלמדינה̈ דׄ[את] אלברגׄ אלשאמךׄ ליגׄתמעוא פיהא ולא יתבדדוא פי אלארץׄ פיסתצ[לחוא]ֿ קיל קד יערץׄ פי אלפעל וגׄוה קבח פיכׄרגׄ מע דׄלך כונה חסנא פיגׄוז אן יכון מא חא[ול]ה האולא אלקום מן בנא אלמד[ינה̈] ואלאגׄתמאע אליהא מפסדה̈ או תרכא אלואגׄב. פלא יסלם חס[נא]
content.english: …people what runs the course of punishment, on account of what they did by way of building the city with the lofty tower, [intending] thereby to gather in it and not be scattered throughout the earth, so as to attain we[lfare]? — It is said: aspects of [moral] ugliness¹ may attach to a deed, [in which case the deed] departs alongside that from being good. So it is admissible that what these people attemp[t]ed by way of building the ci[ty] and gathering to it was a corruption² or an abandonment of the obligatory³, in which case it does not retain its good[ness]…
content.comments: ¹ qubḥ (قبح) — "[moral] ugliness, [ethical] foulness"; the Muʿtazilite-Karaite category of objective moral wrongness, the complement of ḥusn. ² mafsada (مفسدة) — "corruption, [a thing that] produces harm"; the legal-theoretical category of an act that yields net evil. ³ al-wājib (الواجب) — "the obligatory"; the standard uṣūl al-fiqh category for what is religiously required.

content.hebrew: מע דׄלך ואלמקתצׄי להדׄא תקדם אלאמר להם [ב]קולה תעאלי שר[צו] בארץ ור[בו] בה (בראשית ט:ז) ואלמקתצׄי אלסע[ה̈] פי אלארץׄ וא[ל]אבתסאט פיהא ולעלה ק[ד ו]גׄב דׄלך עליהם ופי צׄמנה אלנהי עמא פעלוה מן אלאגׄתמא[ע] פי בק[עה̈ ו]אחדה̈ מן אלארץׄ ה.
content.english: …along with that. And what indicates this is the prior command to them in His (may He be exalted) saying *she[rṣu] va-arets u-r[evu] vah* 'be fr[uitful] in the earth and mul[tiply] in it' (Gen 9:7), which requires expan[sion] in the earth and spread throughout it. And perhaps that was [obli]gatory upon them, and included in its scope is the prohibition against what they did by way of gather[ing] in [one] sin[gle] re[gion] of the earth. End.

content.hebrew: אן קיל מא הו א...בפעלה נסוא מא כאנוא יערפוה מן אללגה̈. פאן כאן פקדהם אלעלם בהא פאלא גׄאז קול מן ידעי אלערפה̈ וכיף יגׄ[ו]ז אן ינסוא מא כאנוא יעלמונה צׄרורה̈ מן אללגה̈ חתי לם יפהם אחד[הם] ען אלאכׄר מא כאן יערפה באלאסם או ליס דׄלך יכמל בכמאל אלעקל ויערף מא ילזמונה למן זעם אן אלאלאם אלמפעולה̈ באלבהימה̈ ואלטפל עקובה̈ להמא עלי מעאצי סלפת מנהמא ולם יעלמא בהא אלאן מן אן דׄלך כאן יודי אלי אן יכון אח[ד]נא כאן אמירא מנדׄ עשרין סנה̈ ואליא עלי אקלים עטׄים תׄם ינסא דׄלך ולא ידׄכרה קיל יגׄוז
content.english: If it be said: what is the […] by His [intervening] deed, they forgot what they knew of the language. If their loss of knowledge of it [is the explanation], then would it not be admissible [to suppose any claim of forgetting]? And how is it admissible that they should forget what they knew of the language by necessity¹, such that none of them understood from another what he had formerly known by name? Or is this not [a knowledge that] is completed by the completeness of intellect, [such that] one knows what is incumbent on [the holders of such knowledge]? — to one who claims that the pains inflicted on the beast and the infant are a punishment upon them for past disobediences of theirs of which they now have no knowledge²: that [claim] would imply that one of us could have been an emir for twenty years, and a governor over a great region, and then forget that and not remember it. It is said: it is admissible…
content.comments: ¹ ḍarūratan (ضرورةً) — "by necessity, [as] indubitable"; the kalām epistemic category of necessary knowledge, contrasted with iktisāb (acquired knowledge). Necessary knowledge cannot be lost without destroying the intellect itself. ² Ali is here glancing at — and rejecting — the transmigration / pre-existent-sin theodicy advanced by some thinkers to account for the suffering of innocents. The analogy is: such a theodicy requires agents to be punished for past acts they cannot remember, which (Ali argues) is incoherent in the same way that erasure of necessarily known facts is incoherent. The pivot to the ṣarfa-polemic in segs. 249–252 plays out the same epistemic argument.

content.hebrew: אן יכון תעאלי אלקי בינהם אלעדאואת ואלמנאפראת אלתי ענדהא קוית דואעיהם אלי בעד כל פריק מנהם ען אלאכׄר ווצׄע לגה̈ לה לא יערפהא גירה. פענד תטאול אלאזמאן עליהם בדׄלך תנאסוא כתׄירהא מן אללגה̈ אלאולי לעדם תכׄאטבהם בהא ולזומהם אלתכׄאטב באלתׄאניה̈ כאלאעגׄמי אלנאקל אלי בלאד אלערב וידום
content.english: …that [He] (may He be exalted) cast among them enmities and antagonisms by which their motives toward [the] mutual distancing of each party from the other were strengthened, and set for [each] a language that the others did not know. So when the times grew long upon them in that, they came to forget much of the first language, for lack of [practicing] speech in it and their cleaving to speech in the second [language] — like the foreigner¹ who removes to the lands of the Arabs and persists…
content.comments: ¹ al-aʿjamī (الأعجمي) — "the foreigner, the non-Arab [speaker]"; the standard Arabic ethnographic-linguistic term.

content.hebrew: סמאעה̈ וכׄטאבה̈ באלערביה̈ מן גיר תכׄאטבה בשי מן אלאעגׄמיה̈. פלא מחאלה̈ [א]נה בעד אלסנין אלכתׄירה̈ ינסא אלכתׄיר מנהא. וליס פי אלקצה̈ מא ידל עלי אן תבדדהם פי אלארץׄ ועדם פהם אחדהם כלאם אלאכׄר
content.english: …in his hearing and being addressed in Arabic, with no address to him in anything of the foreign [language]; so it is without doubt that, after the many years, he will forget most of it. And there is nothing in the narrative to indicate that their dispersal in the earth and the absence of mutual understanding among them…

content.hebrew: כאן פי יום ויומין. פילזם מנה אלקול באלצרפה̈ אלתי מעני הדׄה אללפטׄה̈ ענד מן יקול בהא הו גׄואז אן יצרף תעא[ל]י אלפציח פי אללגה̈ אלבאלג פיהא ען אלעלם במא כאן באלאמס מעאניא לה [ו]דׄלך בחיתׄ [ל]א יפעל פיה אלעלם בה לאן פי דׄלך אכׄלאלא בכמאל [ע]קלה אדׄ דׄלך לו גׄאז לגׄוזנא אן יכון מן יכׄברנא מן חדׄאק אלכתאב ואפצׄלהם פי אלכתאבה̈ אני א[לי]ום לא אערף שיא מנה והו באלאמס ומא קבלה כאן בפוק אהל עצרה פיהא ויכון מע דׄלך צאדקא וקד עלם צׄרורה̈ כדׄבה מתי כאן כאמל אלעקל. וכמא לא יגׄוז אן ינסוא גׄמיע מא כאנוא יעלמונה באלאמס מן אללגה̈ כדׄלך לא יגׄוז אן ינסוא גׄמיעהא בעד אלסנין אלכתׄירה̈ חתי אדׄא קיל
content.english: …happened in a day or two. It follows that there is no [need to invoke] the [divine] deflection¹ — the meaning of this term, according to those who maintain it, is the admissibility that [He] (may He be exalted) divert the eloquent² speaker in a language, the consummate one in it, from the knowledge of what was for him a meaning [only] yesterday, by way of [the divine] not enacting in him the knowledge of it — for in that is a compromising of the completeness of his [in]tellect, since, were that admissible, it would be admissible for us [to suppose that] one of the masters of writing, the most excellent of them in [the art of] writing, should tell us 'I to[d]ay know nothing of it, though yesterday and earlier I was above the people of my era in it' — and that he be [reckoned] truthful at the same time, when his lying is known of necessity, given the completeness of [his] intellect. And just as it is not admissible that they forget all of what they knew yesterday of the language, so it is not admissible that they forget all of it after many years, such that if one were to say…
content.comments: ¹ al-ṣarfa (الصرفة) — "divine deflection, [the] turning-away [of human capacity from a normally-possible act]"; the famous Muʿtazilite doctrine associated with al-Naẓẓām (d. ca. 220–230 AH) that God deflects human ability from producing certain feats — originally used to ground the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qurʾān. Ali rejects ṣarfa as an explanation of the Babel confusion on epistemological grounds: it requires an instantaneous erasure of necessary knowledge incompatible with the completeness of intellect. ² al-faṣīḥ (الفصيح) — "the eloquent, [the] master [of the language]"; the Arabic-rhetoric term for the ideal native speaker.

content.hebrew: לאחדם ממן כאן לגתה תקדירא ערביה̈ אלכׄבז איש הו ויחצׄר בין ידיה רגפאן מנה פיקול לא אעלם לאנה אן גׄאז אן ינסאה ואלחאל הדׄה גׄאז אן יכון מלכא עלי אמם כתׄרה̈ מנדׄ כׄמסין סנה̈ ויפתח אלבלאד אלואסעה̈ וינסי דׄלך ולא ידׄכר מנה שיא ענד סואלה ענה אדׄ ל[י]ס דׄלך גׄאר מגׄרי אלאמור אלמלתבסה̈ בגירהא אלתי יגׄוז נסיאנהא בעד מדה̈ כדכׄול חמאם מכׄצוצה̈ פי יום מכׄצוץ ואשבאהה ה. עלי אן קולה אשר לא ישמעו איש שפת רעהו (בראשית יא:ז) עלי אלתאויל אלמקדם דׄכרה ליס הו ראגׄע אלי אללגה̈ אלתי נשו עליהא בל אלי אללגה̈ אלמתגׄדדה̈ אלתי תואצׄע עליהא אלפריקאן למא באינא אלפרי[ק] אלתׄאלתׄ ודׄלך מטאבק לטׄאהר קולה הבה נרדה ונב׳ ש׳ שפתם וג׳ (בראשית יא:ז).
content.english: …to one of them whose language is, by way of supposing an example¹, Arabic, [if one asked] *al-khubz, aysh huwa?* 'bread, what is it?' — and two loaves of it were presented before him — and he said 'I do not know,' [that would be incoherent]; for if it were admissible that he forget that in such a state, then it would be admissible that he could have been a king over many nations for fifty years and conquered wide lands, and then forgotten that and remembered nothing of it when asked — for this does not run the course of those matters that, being mixed up with others, may admissibly be forgotten after a period (like the entering of a particular bathhouse on a particular day, and the like). End. — Moreover, his saying *asher lo yishmeʿu ish sefat reʿehu* 'so that they shall not understand, each man, the speech of his fellow' (Gen 11:7), on the previously-mentioned interpretation, does not refer back to the language they grew up on, but to the [newly] renewed languages² that the two [remaining] parties agreed upon³ once the third party had separated from us. And that conforms to the apparent sense of his saying *havah neredah ve-na[velah] s[am] sefatam* 'come, let us go down and confuse there their speech' etc. (Gen 11:7).
content.comments: ¹ taqdīran (تقديراً) — "by way of supposing [an example], [hypothetically]"; here the rhetorical hypothetical, not the supplied-reading sense. ² al-lugha al-mutajaddida (اللغة المتجددة) — "the [newly] renewed language"; the new languages that arose to replace the original common tongue. ³ tawāḍaʿa ʿalayhā (تواضع عليها) — "agreed upon [it] [by convention]"; the kalām/uṣūl term for the conventional fixing of linguistic meanings, central to the Karaite/Muʿtazilite doctrine that language is conventional (tawqīf), not divinely set.

content.hebrew: ש[ם] בן מאת שנה ויולד את ארפכשד שנתים אחר המבול – יחתאגׄ אלי תכׄריגׄ לאנה יקול ויהי נ[ח] בן חמש מאות שנה ויולד נח את שם (בראשית ה:לב) וקאל אי[צׄ]א ונח בן שש מאות שנה והמבול היה (בראשית ז:ו) פאקתצׄא מגׄמוע דׄלך כון ולאדה̈ שם לארפכשד פי סנה̈ אלמבול פכיף יקול שנתים אחר המבול. ווגׄה
content.english: **"Sh[em] was one hundred years old when he begot Arpachshad, two years after the Flood"** (*Sh[em] ben meʾat shana va-yoled et Arpakhshad shenatayim aḥar ha-mabbul*). This requires reconciliation¹, for he says *va-yehi N[oaḥ] ben ḥamesh meʾot shana va-yoled Noaḥ et Shem* 'and N[oah] was 500 years old and Noah begot Shem' (Gen 5:32), and he al[s]o said *ve-Noaḥ ben shesh meʾot shana ve-ha-mabbul haya* 'and Noah was 600 years old and the Flood came' (Gen 7:6) — and the combination of that requires that the birth of Arpachshad to Shem would be in the year of the Flood. So how can he say 'two years after the Flood'? And the manner of [the reconciliation]…
content.comments: ¹ takhrīj (تخريج) — "[harmonizing] reconciliation, [the] working-out"; the standard hermeneutical term for resolving an apparent contradiction between scriptural statements by supplying a principled construal.

content.hebrew: אלתכׄריגׄ פי דׄלך הו מן רסם אלכתאב אן יכׄרגׄ בעץׄ סנה̈ בסנה̈ ויכׄרגׄ איצׄא סנה̈ וכסר בסנה̈. אלא תרי אלי קולה פי מלך דויד אולא בן שלשים שנה דוד במלכו ארבעים שנה מלך (שמואל ב׳ ה:ד) בחברון מלך על יהודה שבע שנים וששה חדשים ובירושלים מלך שלשים ושלוש שנה (שמואל ב׳ ה:ה) פדׄכר אן גׄמלה̈ סני מלכה ארבעון סנה̈ ולמא פ[צ]להא זאד ען אלא[רב]עין סתה̈ שהור פחצל אנה אכׄרגׄ אלסנה̈ אלארבעיניה̈ ואלסתה̈ שהור בסנה̈ וקד יפעל עכסא מן דׄלך באן יכׄרגׄ בעץׄ סנה̈ בסנה̈ והו אלמוצׄע אלדׄי נחן נסתתליה. פינבגי אן יכון קולה ויהי נח בן חמש מאות שנה ויולד נח את שם (בראשית ה:לב) אן תכון אלסנה̈ אלאכׄירה̈ מן אלכׄמסמאיה̈ נאקצה̈ וכדׄלך אלסנה̈ אלאכׄירה̈ פי קולה ונח בן שש מאות שנה והמבול היה (בראשית ז:ו) ואן יכון קולה שם בן מאת שנה ויולד את אר[פ]כשד (בראשית יא:י) הי מאיה̈ סנה̈ וכסר. ולם ידׄכר אלכסר כמא לם ידׄכר אלסתה̈ שהור פי סני מלך דויד. פיכון אלכסר אלזאיד ען אלמאיה̈ סנה̈ לשם וקת ולאדה̈ ארפכשד מע אלכסר אלנאקץ ען אלסנה̈ [אל]אכׄירה̈ מן אלסתמאיה̈ סנה̈ אלמדׄכור מגׄי אלטופאן פיהא מן עמר נח מחסובא בסנתין פיואפק דׄלך קולה שנתים אחר המבול (בראשית יא:י) ומדה̈ אלמ[ב]ול ארבעון יומא לא גיר כק׳ ויהי המבול ארבעים יום על הארץ (בראשית ז:יז).
content.english: …of the reconciliation in that, is from the convention¹ of Scripture, [namely] that it brings out part of a year as a [full] year, and brings out also a year and a fraction² as a [full] year. Do you not see his saying about David's kingship initially: *ben sheloshim shana David be-malkho arbaʿim shana malakh* 'David was thirty years old when he reigned; he reigned forty years' (2Sam 5:4), [and:] *be-Ḥevron malakh ʿal Yehuda shevaʿ shanim ve-shisha ḥodashim u-vi-Yrushalayim malakh sheloshim ve-shalosh shana* 'in Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned 33 years' (2Sam 5:5) — so he mentioned that the totality of the years of his reign was 40 years, but when he det[ai]led it, it exceeded the f[or]ty by six months. So what comes out is that he reckoned the year of the 40-mark together with the six months as [one] year. And it sometimes does the converse of that, in that it brings out part of a year as a [full] year — which is the place we are following [here]. So it must be that his saying *va-yehi Noaḥ ben ḥamesh meʾot shana va-yoled Noaḥ et Shem* 'Noah was 500 years old and begot Shem' (Gen 5:32) — that the last year of the 500 is incomplete; and likewise the last year in his saying *ve-Noaḥ ben shesh meʾot shana ve-ha-mabbul haya* 'and Noah was 600 years old and the Flood came' (Gen 7:6); and that his saying *Shem ben meʾat shana va-yoled et Ar[p]akhshad* 'Shem was 100 years old and begot Ar[p]achshad' (Gen 11:10) is 100 years and a fraction. And [Scripture] did not mention the fraction, just as it did not mention the six months in David's reign-years. So the fraction exceeding the 100 years for Shem at the time of Arpachshad's birth, together with the fraction deficient from the [la]st year of the 600 years (the year in which the coming of the Flood is mentioned in Noah's lifetime), reckoned together as two years — and this conforms with his saying 'two years after the Flood' (Gen 11:10). And the duration of the F[l]ood was 40 days, no more, as in [the verse] *va-yehi ha-mabbul arbaʿim yom ʿal ha-arets* 'and the Flood was forty days upon the earth' (Gen 7:17).
content.comments: ¹ rasm (رسم) — "convention, [customary scribal] practice"; here the conventional Scriptural chronographic usage of rounding partial years. ² kasr (كسر) — "fraction, [the] remainder [of a year past a round number]"; the mathematical term, applied here to chronology.

content.hebrew: Gen 12:1
content.english: Gen 12:1

content.hebrew: ויאמר ייי אל אברם לך לך –
content.english: **"And the LORD said to Abram: go forth!"** (*va-yomer YY el Avram lekh-lekha*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion picks up with the next phrase.

content.hebrew: [ק]ולה מארצך וממלודתך ומבית אביך – הו עלי טריק אלתצעיב עליה חתי אדׄא סארע אלי אלאמתתׄאל טׄהרת טאעתה.
content.english: [H]is saying **"from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house"** (*me-arṣekha u-mimoladtekha u-mi-beit avikha*). This is by way of making [the matter] difficult¹ upon him, so that when he hastens to compliance², his obedience may manifest.
content.comments: ¹ al-taṣʿīb (التصعيب) — "making [a matter] difficult, [ratcheting up the] burden"; here the rhetorical-moral device of layering the command (land, kindred, father's house) so that Abraham's prompt compliance displays the depth of his obedience. ² al-imtithāl (الامتثال) — "compliance, [obedient following] of the command"; standard kalām term for the act that fulfills a divine command.

content.hebrew: וקולה אל הארץ אשר אראך – יגׄרי מגׄרי אלמדׄכור איצׄא אדׄ לו קאל לה אמץׄ אלי אלשאם לערף אלגׄהה̈
content.english: And his saying **"to the land that I will show you"** (*el ha-arets asher arʾekha*). This runs the course of what was just mentioned [the deliberate difficulty] — for had He said to him 'go to al-Shām¹', he would have known the direction…
content.comments: ¹ al-Shām (الشام) — the standard medieval Arabic designation for greater Syria, including the land of Israel. Ali uses the contemporary geographic term as the assumed destination of Abraham's migration.

content.hebrew: אלתי יקצדהא מן אול שי וזאל תטלע נפסה אלי מערפה̈ דׄלך פלמא לם ידׄכרהא לה אולא כאן דׄלך עליה שאקא וליס קולה אשר אראך מן תאכׄיר אלביאן פי שי מן חיתׄ אן תאכׄיר אלביאן אלדׄי לא יגׄוז עליה תעאלי הו אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלמגׄמלה̈ פי אללגה̈ אלמפתקרה̈ אלי ביאן יפהם בה גרצׄה בהא פלא יבין. או אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלמוצׄועה̈ פי אללגה̈ לאמר ויריד בהא סואה פלא יבין. או אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלתי להא חקיקה̈ פי אללגה̈ ומגׄאז ויריד אלמגׄאז מן דון אלחקיקה̈ ולא יבין. פהדׄא ואשבאהה [מ]מא לא יגׄוז עלי אלקדים תעאלי תאכׄיר ביאן מראדה בה לאן אלמ[כׄ]אטב ואלחאל הדׄה לא יכון קד פהם מראדה בכׄטאבה והדׄא בנקץ מא קד אסתקר מן כון כׄטאבה סבחאנה דלאלה̈ עלי מראדה.
content.english: …that he intended from the first instance, and his soul would have ceased aspiring to the knowledge of it. So when He did not mention [the destination] to him at the outset, that was burdensome upon him. And his saying *asher arʾekha* 'that I will show you' is not [an instance] of the delaying of clarification¹ in any respect — since the delaying of clarification that is not admissible upon Him (may He be exalted) is [of three kinds]: that He should bring forth in the language an ambiguous expression² requiring clarification by which its purpose is to be understood, and then not clarify; or that He should bring forth an expression set in the language for [one] matter and intend by it another, and not clarify; or that He should bring forth an expression that has a literal sense³ and a figurative sense⁴ in the language, and intend the figurative without the literal, and not clarify. So this and the like [are] [a]mong that for which it is not admissible that the Eternal (may He be exalted) delay the clarification of His intent thereby — for the add[r]essee, in such a state, would not have understood His intent by His address, and this contradicts what is established, that His address (praise be to Him) is a [conventional] indication⁵ of His intent.
content.comments: ¹ taʾkhīr al-bayān (تأخير البيان) — "delaying of clarification, [postponement of] explication"; the uṣūl al-fiqh problem of whether a divine pronouncement may issue ambiguously and only later be clarified. The Karaites and the Muʿtazila reject this in the strong form: any ambiguity at the time-of-need (waqt al-ḥāja) would amount to deception. ² al-ʿibāra al-mujmala (العبارة المجملة) — "the ambiguous / [semantically] underdetermined expression"; the uṣūl term for a formulation whose intent cannot be fixed from the expression alone. ³ ḥaqīqa (حقيقة) — "literal sense, [conventionally fixed] meaning"; the standard Arabic-rhetoric/uṣūl term for the primary lexical sense of an expression. ⁴ majāz (مجاز) — "figurative sense, [transferred] meaning"; the rhetorical/uṣūl term for the metaphorical or extended sense, the standard contrast to ḥaqīqa. ⁵ dalāla (دلالة) — "[conventional] indication"; the kalām/uṣūl term for the relation by which an expression indicates its meaning. Ali's point: that relation is constitutive of divine speech, so God cannot speak ambiguously where comprehension is required.

content.hebrew: פקולה אל הארץ אשר אראך – מע[נאה פ]י [גׄ]מיע דׄלך מן חיתׄ אן אברהם עליה אלסלם קד פהם בהא מראדה גׄמלה̈ והו אלמרור מן ארצׄה אלי ארץׄ סואהא סיערפה בהא תפצילא. [ול]א יגׄוז מע דׄלך אן יכון מראדה באלעבארה̈ אלתי אורדהא בנא מדׄבח ותקר[יב] קראבין עליה ה.
content.english: [So] his saying **"to the land that I will show you"** (*el ha-arets asher arʾekha*). [Its] mean[ing in al]l [that], inasmuch as Abraham (peace be upon him) had understood His intent by it in general¹ — namely, the [act of] travelling from his land to a land other than it, which He would [later] inform him of in detail². And it is [not] admissible, along with that, that His intent by the expression which He brought forth was the building of an altar and the off[er]ing of sacrifices upon it. End.
content.comments: ¹ jumlatan (جملةً) — "in general, [holistically, in the aggregate]"; the standard uṣūl complement to tafṣīlan. ² tafṣīlan (تفصيلاً) — "in detail, [in the particulars]"; the complement to jumlatan.
