And perhaps that was [obli]gatory upon them, and included in its scope is the prohibition against what they did by way of gather[ing] in [one] sin[gle] re[gion] of the earth. End.

content.hebrew: אן קיל מא הו א...בפעלה נסוא מא כאנוא יערפוה מן אללגה̈. פאן כאן פקדהם אלעלם בהא פאלא גׄאז קול מן ידעי אלערפה̈ וכיף יגׄ[ו]ז אן ינסוא מא כאנוא יעלמונה צׄרורה̈ מן אללגה̈ חתי לם יפהם אחד[הם] ען אלאכׄר מא כאן יערפה באלאסם או ליס דׄלך יכמל בכמאל אלעקל ויערף מא ילזמונה למן זעם אן אלאלאם אלמפעולה̈ באלבהימה̈ ואלטפל עקובה̈ להמא עלי מעאצי סלפת מנהמא ולם יעלמא בהא אלאן מן אן דׄלך כאן יודי אלי אן יכון אח[ד]נא כאן אמירא מנדׄ עשרין סנה̈ ואליא עלי אקלים עטׄים תׄם ינסא דׄלך ולא ידׄכרה קיל יגׄוז
content.english: If it be said: what is the […] by His [intervening] deed, they forgot what they knew of the language. If their loss of knowledge of it [is the explanation], then would it not be admissible [to suppose any claim of forgetting]? And how is it admissible that they should forget what they knew of the language by necessity¹, such that none of them understood from another what he had formerly known by name? Or is this not [a knowledge that] is completed by the completeness of intellect, [such that] one knows what is incumbent on [the holders of such knowledge]? — to one who claims that the pains inflicted on the beast and the infant are a punishment upon them for past disobediences of theirs of which they now have no knowledge²: that [claim] would imply that one of us could have been an emir for twenty years, and a governor over a great region, and then forget that and not remember it. It is said: it is admissible…
content.comments: ¹ ḍarūratan (ضرورةً) — "by necessity, [as] indubitable"; the kalām epistemic category of necessary knowledge, contrasted with iktisāb (acquired knowledge). Necessary knowledge cannot be lost without destroying the intellect itself. ² Ali is here glancing at — and rejecting — the transmigration / pre-existent-sin theodicy advanced by some thinkers to account for the suffering of innocents. The analogy is: such a theodicy requires agents to be punished for past acts they cannot remember, which (Ali argues) is incoherent in the same way that erasure of necessarily known facts is incoherent. The pivot to the ṣarfa-polemic in segs. 249–252 plays out the same epistemic argument.

content.hebrew: אן יכון תעאלי אלקי בינהם אלעדאואת ואלמנאפראת אלתי ענדהא קוית דואעיהם אלי בעד כל פריק מנהם ען אלאכׄר ווצׄע לגה̈ לה לא יערפהא גירה. פענד תטאול אלאזמאן עליהם בדׄלך תנאסוא כתׄירהא מן אללגה̈ אלאולי לעדם תכׄאטבהם בהא ולזומהם אלתכׄאטב באלתׄאניה̈ כאלאעגׄמי אלנאקל אלי בלאד אלערב וידום
content.english: …that [He] (may He be exalted) cast among them enmities and antagonisms by which their motives toward [the] mutual distancing of each party from the other were strengthened, and set for [each] a language that the others did not know. So when the times grew long upon them in that, they came to forget much of the first language, for lack of [practicing] speech in it and their cleaving to speech in the second [language] — like the foreigner¹ who removes to the lands of the Arabs and persists…
content.comments: ¹ al-aʿjamī (الأعجمي) — "the foreigner, the non-Arab [speaker]"; the standard Arabic ethnographic-linguistic term.

content.hebrew: סמאעה̈ וכׄטאבה̈ באלערביה̈ מן גיר תכׄאטבה בשי מן אלאעגׄמיה̈. פלא מחאלה̈ [א]נה בעד אלסנין אלכתׄירה̈ ינסא אלכתׄיר מנהא. וליס פי אלקצה̈ מא ידל עלי אן תבדדהם פי אלארץׄ ועדם פהם אחדהם כלאם אלאכׄר
content.english: …in his hearing and being addressed in Arabic, with no address to him in anything of the foreign [language]; so it is without doubt that, after the many years, he will forget most of it. And there is nothing in the narrative to indicate that their dispersal in the earth and the absence of mutual understanding among them…

content.hebrew: כאן פי יום ויומין. פילזם מנה אלקול באלצרפה̈ אלתי מעני הדׄה אללפטׄה̈ ענד מן יקול בהא הו גׄואז אן יצרף תעא[ל]י אלפציח פי אללגה̈ אלבאלג פיהא ען אלעלם במא כאן באלאמס מעאניא לה [ו]דׄלך בחיתׄ [ל]א יפעל פיה אלעלם בה לאן פי דׄלך אכׄלאלא בכמאל [ע]קלה אדׄ דׄלך לו גׄאז לגׄוזנא אן יכון מן יכׄברנא מן חדׄאק אלכתאב ואפצׄלהם פי אלכתאבה̈ אני א[לי]ום לא אערף שיא מנה והו באלאמס ומא קבלה כאן בפוק אהל עצרה פיהא ויכון מע דׄלך צאדקא וקד עלם צׄרורה̈ כדׄבה מתי כאן כאמל אלעקל. וכמא לא יגׄוז אן ינסוא גׄמיע מא כאנוא יעלמונה באלאמס מן אללגה̈ כדׄלך לא יגׄוז אן ינסוא גׄמיעהא בעד אלסנין אלכתׄירה̈ חתי אדׄא קיל
content.english: …happened in a day or two. It follows that there is no [need to invoke] the [divine] deflection¹ — the meaning of this term, according to those who maintain it, is the admissibility that [He] (may He be exalted) divert the eloquent² speaker in a language, the consummate one in it, from the knowledge of what was for him a meaning [only] yesterday, by way of [the divine] not enacting in him the knowledge of it — for in that is a compromising of the completeness of his [in]tellect, since, were that admissible, it would be admissible for us [to suppose that] one of the masters of writing, the most excellent of them in [the art of] writing, should tell us 'I to[d]ay know nothing of it, though yesterday and earlier I was above the people of my era in it' — and that he be [reckoned] truthful at the same time, when his lying is known of necessity, given the completeness of [his] intellect. And just as it is not admissible that they forget all of what they knew yesterday of the language, so it is not admissible that they forget all of it after many years, such that if one were to say…
content.comments: ¹ al-ṣarfa (الصرفة) — "divine deflection, [the] turning-away [of human capacity from a normally-possible act]"; the famous Muʿtazilite doctrine associated with al-Naẓẓām (d. ca. 220–230 AH) that God deflects human ability from producing certain feats — originally used to ground the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qurʾān. Ali rejects ṣarfa as an explanation of the Babel confusion on epistemological grounds: it requires an instantaneous erasure of necessary knowledge incompatible with the completeness of intellect. ² al-faṣīḥ (الفصيح) — "the eloquent, [the] master [of the language]"; the Arabic-rhetoric term for the ideal native speaker.

content.hebrew: לאחדם ממן כאן לגתה תקדירא ערביה̈ אלכׄבז איש הו ויחצׄר בין ידיה רגפאן מנה פיקול לא אעלם לאנה אן גׄאז אן ינסאה ואלחאל הדׄה גׄאז אן יכון מלכא עלי אמם כתׄרה̈ מנדׄ כׄמסין סנה̈ ויפתח אלבלאד אלואסעה̈ וינסי דׄלך ולא ידׄכר מנה שיא ענד סואלה ענה אדׄ ל[י]ס דׄלך גׄאר מגׄרי אלאמור אלמלתבסה̈ בגירהא אלתי יגׄוז נסיאנהא בעד מדה̈ כדכׄול חמאם מכׄצוצה̈ פי יום מכׄצוץ ואשבאהה ה. עלי אן קולה אשר לא ישמעו איש שפת רעהו (בראשית יא:ז) עלי אלתאויל אלמקדם דׄכרה ליס הו ראגׄע אלי אללגה̈ אלתי נשו עליהא בל אלי אללגה̈ אלמתגׄדדה̈ אלתי תואצׄע עליהא אלפריקאן למא באינא אלפרי[ק] אלתׄאלתׄ ודׄלך מטאבק לטׄאהר קולה הבה נרדה ונב׳ ש׳ שפתם וג׳ (בראשית יא:ז).
content.english: …to one of them whose language is, by way of supposing an example¹, Arabic, [if one asked] *al-khubz, aysh huwa?* 'bread, what is it?' — and two loaves of it were presented before him — and he said 'I do not know,' [that would be incoherent]; for if it were admissible that he forget that in such a state, then it would be admissible that he could have been a king over many nations for fifty years and conquered wide lands, and then forgotten that and remembered nothing of it when asked — for this does not run the course of those matters that, being mixed up with others, may admissibly be forgotten after a period (like the entering of a particular bathhouse on a particular day, and the like). End. — Moreover, his saying *asher lo yishmeʿu ish sefat reʿehu* 'so that they shall not understand, each man, the speech of his fellow' (Gen 11:7), on the previously-mentioned interpretation, does not refer back to the language they grew up on, but to the [newly] renewed languages² that the two [remaining] parties agreed upon³ once the third party had separated from us. And that conforms to the apparent sense of his saying *havah neredah ve-na[velah] s[am] sefatam* 'come, let us go down and confuse there their speech' etc. (Gen 11:7).
content.comments: ¹ taqdīran (تقديراً) — "by way of supposing [an example], [hypothetically]"; here the rhetorical hypothetical, not the supplied-reading sense. ² al-lugha al-mutajaddida (اللغة المتجددة) — "the [newly] renewed language"; the new languages that arose to replace the original common tongue. ³ tawāḍaʿa ʿalayhā (تواضع عليها) — "agreed upon [it] [by convention]"; the kalām/uṣūl term for the conventional fixing of linguistic meanings, central to the Karaite/Muʿtazilite doctrine that language is conventional (tawqīf), not divinely set.

content.hebrew: ש[ם] בן מאת שנה ויולד את ארפכשד שנתים אחר המבול – יחתאגׄ אלי תכׄריגׄ לאנה יקול ויהי נ[ח] בן חמש מאות שנה ויולד נח את שם (בראשית ה:לב) וקאל אי[צׄ]א ונח בן שש מאות שנה והמבול היה (בראשית ז:ו) פאקתצׄא מגׄמוע דׄלך כון ולאדה̈ שם לארפכשד פי סנה̈ אלמבול פכיף יקול שנתים אחר המבול. ווגׄה
content.english: **"Sh[em] was one hundred years old when he begot Arpachshad, two years after the Flood"** (*Sh[em] ben meʾat shana va-yoled et Arpakhshad shenatayim aḥar ha-mabbul*). This requires reconciliation¹, for he says *va-yehi N[oaḥ] ben ḥamesh meʾot shana va-yoled Noaḥ et Shem* 'and N[oah] was 500 years old and Noah begot Shem' (Gen 5:32), and he al[s]o said *ve-Noaḥ ben shesh meʾot shana ve-ha-mabbul haya* 'and Noah was 600 years old and the Flood came' (Gen 7:6) — and the combination of that requires that the birth of Arpachshad to Shem would be in the year of the Flood. So how can he say 'two years after the Flood'? And the manner of [the reconciliation]…
content.comments: ¹ takhrīj (تخريج) — "[harmonizing] reconciliation, [the] working-out"; the standard hermeneutical term for resolving an apparent contradiction between scriptural statements by supplying a principled construal.

content.hebrew: אלתכׄריגׄ פי דׄלך הו מן רסם אלכתאב אן יכׄרגׄ בעץׄ סנה̈ בסנה̈ ויכׄרגׄ איצׄא סנה̈ וכסר בסנה̈. אלא תרי אלי קולה פי מלך דויד אולא בן שלשים שנה דוד במלכו ארבעים שנה מלך (שמואל ב׳ ה:ד) בחברון מלך על יהודה שבע שנים וששה חדשים ובירושלים מלך שלשים ושלוש שנה (שמואל ב׳ ה:ה) פדׄכר אן גׄמלה̈ סני מלכה ארבעון סנה̈ ולמא פ[צ]להא זאד ען אלא[רב]עין סתה̈ שהור פחצל אנה אכׄרגׄ אלסנה̈ אלארבעיניה̈ ואלסתה̈ שהור בסנה̈ וקד יפעל עכסא מן דׄלך באן יכׄרגׄ בעץׄ סנה̈ בסנה̈ והו אלמוצׄע אלדׄי נחן נסתתליה. פינבגי אן יכון קולה ויהי נח בן חמש מאות שנה ויולד נח את שם (בראשית ה:לב) אן תכון אלסנה̈ אלאכׄירה̈ מן אלכׄמסמאיה̈ נאקצה̈ וכדׄלך אלסנה̈ אלאכׄירה̈ פי קולה ונח בן שש מאות שנה והמבול היה (בראשית ז:ו) ואן יכון קולה שם בן מאת שנה ויולד את אר[פ]כשד (בראשית יא:י) הי מאיה̈ סנה̈ וכסר. ולם ידׄכר אלכסר כמא לם ידׄכר אלסתה̈ שהור פי סני מלך דויד. פיכון אלכסר אלזאיד ען אלמאיה̈ סנה̈ לשם וקת ולאדה̈ ארפכשד מע אלכסר אלנאקץ ען אלסנה̈ [אל]אכׄירה̈ מן אלסתמאיה̈ סנה̈ אלמדׄכור מגׄי אלטופאן פיהא מן עמר נח מחסובא בסנתין פיואפק דׄלך קולה שנתים אחר המבול (בראשית יא:י) ומדה̈ אלמ[ב]ול ארבעון יומא לא גיר כק׳ ויהי המבול ארבעים יום על הארץ (בראשית ז:יז).
content.english: …of the reconciliation in that, is from the convention¹ of Scripture, [namely] that it brings out part of a year as a [full] year, and brings out also a year and a fraction² as a [full] year. Do you not see his saying about David's kingship initially: *ben sheloshim shana David be-malkho arbaʿim shana malakh* 'David was thirty years old when he reigned; he reigned forty years' (2Sam 5:4), [and:] *be-Ḥevron malakh ʿal Yehuda shevaʿ shanim ve-shisha ḥodashim u-vi-Yrushalayim malakh sheloshim ve-shalosh shana* 'in Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned 33 years' (2Sam 5:5) — so he mentioned that the totality of the years of his reign was 40 years, but when he det[ai]led it, it exceeded the f[or]ty by six months. So what comes out is that he reckoned the year of the 40-mark together with the six months as [one] year. And it sometimes does the converse of that, in that it brings out part of a year as a [full] year — which is the place we are following [here]. So it must be that his saying *va-yehi Noaḥ ben ḥamesh meʾot shana va-yoled Noaḥ et Shem* 'Noah was 500 years old and begot Shem' (Gen 5:32) — that the last year of the 500 is incomplete; and likewise the last year in his saying *ve-Noaḥ ben shesh meʾot shana ve-ha-mabbul haya* 'and Noah was 600 years old and the Flood came' (Gen 7:6); and that his saying *Shem ben meʾat shana va-yoled et Ar[p]akhshad* 'Shem was 100 years old and begot Ar[p]achshad' (Gen 11:10) is 100 years and a fraction. And [Scripture] did not mention the fraction, just as it did not mention the six months in David's reign-years. So the fraction exceeding the 100 years for Shem at the time of Arpachshad's birth, together with the fraction deficient from the [la]st year of the 600 years (the year in which the coming of the Flood is mentioned in Noah's lifetime), reckoned together as two years — and this conforms with his saying 'two years after the Flood' (Gen 11:10). And the duration of the F[l]ood was 40 days, no more, as in [the verse] *va-yehi ha-mabbul arbaʿim yom ʿal ha-arets* 'and the Flood was forty days upon the earth' (Gen 7:17).
content.comments: ¹ rasm (رسم) — "convention, [customary scribal] practice"; here the conventional Scriptural chronographic usage of rounding partial years. ² kasr (كسر) — "fraction, [the] remainder [of a year past a round number]"; the mathematical term, applied here to chronology.

content.hebrew: Gen 12:1
content.english: Gen 12:1

content.hebrew: ויאמר ייי אל אברם לך לך –
content.english: **"And the LORD said to Abram: go forth!"** (*va-yomer YY el Avram lekh-lekha*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion picks up with the next phrase.

content.hebrew: [ק]ולה מארצך וממלודתך ומבית אביך – הו עלי טריק אלתצעיב עליה חתי אדׄא סארע אלי אלאמתתׄאל טׄהרת טאעתה.
content.english: [H]is saying **"from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house"** (*me-arṣekha u-mimoladtekha u-mi-beit avikha*). This is by way of making [the matter] difficult¹ upon him, so that when he hastens to compliance², his obedience may manifest.
content.comments: ¹ al-taṣʿīb (التصعيب) — "making [a matter] difficult, [ratcheting up the] burden"; here the rhetorical-moral device of layering the command (land, kindred, father's house) so that Abraham's prompt compliance displays the depth of his obedience. ² al-imtithāl (الامتثال) — "compliance, [obedient following] of the command"; standard kalām term for the act that fulfills a divine command.

content.hebrew: וקולה אל הארץ אשר אראך – יגׄרי מגׄרי אלמדׄכור איצׄא אדׄ לו קאל לה אמץׄ אלי אלשאם לערף אלגׄהה̈
content.english: And his saying **"to the land that I will show you"** (*el ha-arets asher arʾekha*). This runs the course of what was just mentioned [the deliberate difficulty] — for had He said to him 'go to al-Shām¹', he would have known the direction…
content.comments: ¹ al-Shām (الشام) — the standard medieval Arabic designation for greater Syria, including the land of Israel. Ali uses the contemporary geographic term as the assumed destination of Abraham's migration.

content.hebrew: אלתי יקצדהא מן אול שי וזאל תטלע נפסה אלי מערפה̈ דׄלך פלמא לם ידׄכרהא לה אולא כאן דׄלך עליה שאקא וליס קולה אשר אראך מן תאכׄיר אלביאן פי שי מן חיתׄ אן תאכׄיר אלביאן אלדׄי לא יגׄוז עליה תעאלי הו אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלמגׄמלה̈ פי אללגה̈ אלמפתקרה̈ אלי ביאן יפהם בה גרצׄה בהא פלא יבין. או אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלמוצׄועה̈ פי אללגה̈ לאמר ויריד בהא סואה פלא יבין. או אן יורד אלעבארה̈ אלתי להא חקיקה̈ פי אללגה̈ ומגׄאז ויריד אלמגׄאז מן דון אלחקיקה̈ ולא יבין. פהדׄא ואשבאהה [מ]מא לא יגׄוז עלי אלקדים תעאלי תאכׄיר ביאן מראדה בה לאן אלמ[כׄ]אטב ואלחאל הדׄה לא יכון קד פהם מראדה בכׄטאבה והדׄא בנקץ מא קד אסתקר מן כון כׄטאבה סבחאנה דלאלה̈ עלי מראדה.
content.english: …that he intended from the first instance, and his soul would have ceased aspiring to the knowledge of it. So when He did not mention [the destination] to him at the outset, that was burdensome upon him. And his saying *asher arʾekha* 'that I will show you' is not [an instance] of the delaying of clarification¹ in any respect — since the delaying of clarification that is not admissible upon Him (may He be exalted) is [of three kinds]: that He should bring forth in the language an ambiguous expression² requiring clarification by which its purpose is to be understood, and then not clarify; or that He should bring forth an expression set in the language for [one] matter and intend by it another, and not clarify; or that He should bring forth an expression that has a literal sense³ and a figurative sense⁴ in the language, and intend the figurative without the literal, and not clarify. So this and the like [are] [a]mong that for which it is not admissible that the Eternal (may He be exalted) delay the clarification of His intent thereby — for the add[r]essee, in such a state, would not have understood His intent by His address, and this contradicts what is established, that His address (praise be to Him) is a [conventional] indication⁵ of His intent.
content.comments: ¹ taʾkhīr al-bayān (تأخير البيان) — "delaying of clarification, [postponement of] explication"; the uṣūl al-fiqh problem of whether a divine pronouncement may issue ambiguously and only later be clarified. The Karaites and the Muʿtazila reject this in the strong form: any ambiguity at the time-of-need (waqt al-ḥāja) would amount to deception. ² al-ʿibāra al-mujmala (العبارة المجملة) — "the ambiguous / [semantically] underdetermined expression"; the uṣūl term for a formulation whose intent cannot be fixed from the expression alone. ³ ḥaqīqa (حقيقة) — "literal sense, [conventionally fixed] meaning"; the standard Arabic-rhetoric/uṣūl term for the primary lexical sense of an expression. ⁴ majāz (مجاز) — "figurative sense, [transferred] meaning"; the rhetorical/uṣūl term for the metaphorical or extended sense, the standard contrast to ḥaqīqa. ⁵ dalāla (دلالة) — "[conventional] indication"; the kalām/uṣūl term for the relation by which an expression indicates its meaning. Ali's point: that relation is constitutive of divine speech, so God cannot speak ambiguously where comprehension is required.

content.hebrew: פקולה אל הארץ אשר אראך – מע[נאה פ]י [גׄ]מיע דׄלך מן חיתׄ אן אברהם עליה אלסלם קד פהם בהא מראדה גׄמלה̈ והו אלמרור מן ארצׄה אלי ארץׄ סואהא סיערפה בהא תפצילא. [ול]א יגׄוז מע דׄלך אן יכון מראדה באלעבארה̈ אלתי אורדהא בנא מדׄבח ותקר[יב] קראבין עליה ה.
content.english: [So] his saying **"to the land that I will show you"** (*el ha-arets asher arʾekha*). [Its] mean[ing in al]l [that], inasmuch as Abraham (peace be upon him) had understood His intent by it in general¹ — namely, the [act of] travelling from his land to a land other than it, which He would [later] inform him of in detail². And it is [not] admissible, along with that, that His intent by the expression which He brought forth was the building of an altar and the off[er]ing of sacrifices upon it. End.
content.comments: ¹ jumlatan (جملةً) — "in general, [holistically, in the aggregate]"; the standard uṣūl complement to tafṣīlan. ² tafṣīlan (تفصيلاً) — "in detail, [in the particulars]"; the complement to jumlatan. Ali's solution: the destination was given in general at the time of the command, and the requirement of full comprehension is satisfied at that level — the particulars could legitimately await the journey.

content.hebrew: Gen 15:8
content.english: Gen 15:8

content.hebrew: ויאמר יי אלהים במה אדע כי אירשנה – בעד תקדם קולה לה לא יירשך זה כי אם אשר יצא ממעיך הוא יירשך (בראשית טו:ד) ואכׄ[בר] ענה בקולה וה[א]מין ביי (בראשית טו:ו). קיל אן אלגרץׄ בה אלתמאס מא מעה ירתפע תגׄויזה כון הדׄא אלועד באסתתׄני אדׄ קד יעד עז וגׄל ויתואעד ויכון דׄלך באסתתׄני כקולה ליחזקיהו כי מת אתה ולא תחיה (ישעיהו לח:א) ולם ימת פי ת[ל]ך אלעלה̈ מן חיתׄ כאן הדׄא אלכׄבר באסתתׄני אן יצלי ויסלה עז וגׄל פי אלחיאה̈ וכקולה עוד ארבעים יום ונינוה נהפכת (יונה ג:ד) וכאן דׄלך מסתתׄני בצומהם ותובתהם ודעאהם אליה. וכדׄלך גׄוז אברהם אן יכון קולה תעאלי לה לך אתננה ולזרעך (בראשית יג:טו) באסתתׄני פטלב מא יומנה מן דׄלך. ואעלם אן אלקדים סבחאנה לא יגׄוז אן יכׄבר כׄברא ועדא כאן אם ועיד אם גיר [דׄ]לך ויכון פיה אסתתׄני אלא ויגׄב אן יתׄבתה לאן כׄטאבה עז וגׄל דלאלה̈ פמתי כא[ן] פיה אסתתׄני ושרט לא ידׄכרה פי אלוקת לם תח[צ]ל אלתׄקה̈ בכׄברה. וכׄר[גׄ מ]ן כונה דלאלה̈ ואלחאל פימא ילתמסה אלעבד מנה תעאלי לנזול בה אלאסתתני כאלחאל פי אלכׄבר אלאול פי אנה אן לם [יח]צל אליקין בכׄברה אולא בל יגׄוז פיה אסתתׄני לא ינטק בה לם יחצל [אי]צׄא פימא ירפעה בה כׄברא כאן דׄלך איצׄא אם עהדא פלא יחצל קט אלמכׄבר ואלחאל הדׄה [ע]לי תׄקה̈ מן אכׄבארה תעאלי אלמבתדא מנהא ואלמוכד בה. אלא תרי אן אלואחד מנא למא גׄוזנא עליה אלכדׄב פי כׄברה גׄוזנא עלי[ה] אלכדׄב איצׄא פימא יוכד בה כׄברה מן ימין וגירהא פלמא פארק אלקדים תעאלי אחדנא פי הדׄה אלקצׄיה̈ לכונה חכימא וגׄב אן יכון כׄטאבה דלאלה̈ מ[ב]תדא [כא]ן אם מוכדא. ואדׄא כאן דׄלך כדׄלך פקד קטע אברהם עליה אלסלם עלי חצול אלארץׄ לנסלה מיראתׄא מן אלכׄבר אלאול ואנמא אלתמס בקולה במה אדע כי אירשנה (בראשית טו:ח) מא י[כ]ון תאכידא ללכׄבר אלאול בדׄלך מן עהד יקטעה עליה. ואדׄא חסן מנה עז וגׄל אן יבתדי בתואכיד אכׄבארה שי בעד שי ליכון אלמועוד אסכן נפסא חסן מן אלמכלף אלתמאס דׄלך מנה ואלדׄי ינבי ען אנה עליה אלסלם אלתמס מא הדׄא סביל[ה] מנה עז וגׄל בקולה במה אדע כי אירש׳ (בראשית טו:ח) הו מא ורד עקיבה̈ מן קולה ויאמר אליו קחה לי עגלה מש׳ וג׳ (בראשית טו:ט) ה.
content.english: **"And he said: O LORD God, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?"** (*va-yomer YY Elohim ba-mah edaʿ ki irashennah*). After His prior saying to him *lo yirashkha zeh ki im asher yeṣe mi-meʿekha hu yirashkha* 'this one shall not inherit you; rather, the one who issues from your loins, he shall inherit you' (Gen 15:4), and the [Scripture's] re[port] of him in his saying *ve-he[ʾe]min b-YY* 'and he be[liev]ed in the LORD' (Gen 15:6) — it is said: the purpose of [this question] is the seeking out of what, alongside [the promise], removes the admissibility that this promise is [given] under an unstated condition¹ — for [God] (mighty and majestic) sometimes promises and threatens with that under an unstated condition, as in his saying to Hezekiah *ki met atta ve-lo tiḥyeh* 'for you are [as] dead, and shall not live' (Isa 38:1), and he did not die in t[ha]t illness, inasmuch as this report was under the unstated condition that he should pray and entreat [Him], mighty and majestic, for life; and as in his saying *ʿod arbaʿim yom ve-Nineweh nehpaket* 'in another forty days Nineveh shall be overturned' (Jonah 3:4), where that was conditioned upon their fasting and their repentance and their supplication to Him. So in the same way Abraham held it admissible that His (may He be exalted) saying to him *lekha etnennah u-le-zarʿakha* 'to you I shall give it, and to your seed' (Gen 13:15) was under an unstated condition, so he sought out what would secure him from that. — Know, however, that it is not admissible that the Eternal (praise be to Him) should issue a report — be it a promise, a threat, or other than [t]hat — that contains an unstated condition, except that He must [then] confirm² it, since His (mighty and majestic) address is a [conventional] indication³; for whenever there is in it an unstated condition and a stipulation that He does not mention at the time, no confi[de]nce in His report is es[ta]blished, and it exits from being an indication. And likewise the case in what the servant seeks of Him (may He be exalted) for the [explicit] lifting of the implicit condition⁴, which [is on the same footing] as the case in the first report: that if certainty has not been [obtai]ned in His report initially — but rather it [might] admit an unstated condition that is not [overtly] expressed — then [certainty] is [a]lso not obtained in whatever He raises [the doubt] with by report; and the same goes if that be by [a] covenant. So the report-recipient would never come to confidence in such a state, in His (may He be exalted) reports — neither in the initial ones nor in the confirmatory ones. Do you not see that when we [hu]mans hold it admissible that one of us should lie in his report, we hold it [equally] admissible that he should lie also in what he confirms his report with — by oath and otherwise. So when the Eternal (may He be exalted) parts from one of us in this matter, by virtue of His being wise, His address must be an [unambiguous] indication, whether [it] be [i]nitial or confirmatory. And since that is so, Abraham (peace be upon him) had [already] decided [as certain] the [eventual] obtaining of the land for his offspring as an inheritance from the first report; and what he was seeking out by his saying *ba-mah edaʿ ki irashennah* 'by what shall I know that I shall inherit it' (Gen 15:8) is [only] what would [b]e a confirmation of the first report by that means — [some] covenant He would conclude with him. And since it is [deemed] good of Him (mighty and majestic) to begin confirming His reports thing after thing, in order that the one promised may have his soul more at rest, it is [likewise] good of the morally accountable agent⁵ to seek that of Him. And what gives indication that he (peace be upon him) was seeking just this from Him (mighty and majestic) by his saying *ba-mah edaʿ ki ira[shennah]* (Gen 15:8) is what came in immediate succession of his saying *va-yomer elav qeḥa li ʿeglah meshu[lleshet]* 'and He said to him: take me a heifer thr[ee years old]' etc. (Gen 15:9). End.
content.comments: ¹ istithnāʾ (استثناء) — "[an] unstated condition, [implicit] exception"; the uṣūl al-fiqh term for an unspoken qualifying clause that, if operative, would restrict an otherwise unconditional pronouncement. ² thabbata (ثبَّت) — "to confirm, establish"; the form-II verb of th-b-t. ³ See glossary s.v. dalāla. ⁴ nuzūl al-istithnāʾ (نزول الاستثناء) — "the [explicit] discharging / lifting of the [implicit] exception"; the act by which the speaker confirms that no unstated condition is in play. ⁵ al-mukallaf (المكلَّف) — "the morally accountable agent, [the one] subject to taklīf"; the standard kalām designation for the human under religious obligation.

content.hebrew: ועבדום וענו אותם – יריד אן זרעך יכׄד[מו]א אהל תלך אלארץׄ ואהל תלך אלארץׄ ישקוהם תמאם ארבע
content.english: **"And they shall serve them and they shall afflict them"** (*va-ʿavadum ve-ʿinnu otam*). He intends: that your seed shall ser[v]e the people of that land, and the people of that land shall afflict them, for the completion of fou[r]…

content.hebrew: מאיה̈ סנה̈ ולא יגׄוז אן יכון תפסיר ועבדום ויסתכׄ[דמונ]הם פיכון מתעדיא לאן אלמתעדי מן דׄלך פי אלעבראני [יג]י עלי וגׄ[ה]ין אחדהמא אן יתעדי בבא מתׄל כי עבדו בם גם המה (ירמיהו כה:יד). לא ת[עבד] בו עבודת עבד (ויקרא כה:לט) ואלאכׄר מא י[כ]ון אמרה העבד העביד את חילו (יחזקאל כט:יח). ויעבידו מצרים (שמות א:יג). מעבידים אותם (שמות ו:ה). ועבדום ליס מן הדׄין אלצׄרבין בל ממא הו גיר מתעדי מתל ועבדו לעולם (שמות כא:ו) ה. ולא יגׄוז אן תכון מדה̈ אלאסתכׄדאם ואלאשקא ארבע מאיה̈ סנה̈ אדׄ ל[ם] יקימוא במ[צ]ר ארבע מאיה̈ סנה̈ בל כאן מקאמהם בהא מאיתין ועשר סנין מן גׄמלתהא אלענוי חול תׄמאנין סנ[ה̈] מן חין עמר אלרסול עליה אלסלם ואבתדא הדׄה אלארבע מאיה̈ ס[נ]ה̈ היא סנה̈ ולאדה̈ יצחק. אלא תרי אנה ולד לה יעקב ו[הו מ]ן עמרה סתין סנה̈ כקולה ויצחק בן ששים שנה בלדת אותם (בראשית כה:כו) וכאן עמר יעקב ענד דכׄולה אלי מצר מאיה̈ ותׄלתׄין סנה̈ כקולה לפרעה ימי שני מגורי שלושים ומאת שנה (בראשית מז:ט) צאר אלגׄמיע [מ]איה̈ ותסעין סנה̈ יבקא מן אלארבע מאיה̈ מאיתי ועשר סנין הי מדה̈ מקאמהם במצר ה
content.english: …hundred years. And it is not admissible that the interpretation of *va-ʿavadum* be *yastakh[dimū]hum* 'they shall employ them [as servants]'¹, [making the verb] transitive², since the transitive of that in Hebrew [c]omes in two manners. The one of them is that it is transitivized by [the preposition] *bet*, as in *ki ʿavdu vam gam hemma* 'for they too served-with [= enslaved] them' (Jer 25:14), [and] *lo t[aʿavod] bo ʿavodat ʿaved* 'you shall not s[erve-with] him the service of a slave' (Lev 25:39). And the other is what [h]as its imperative [in the heʿevid pattern]: *ha-ʿaved heʿevid et ḥeylo* 'he made his army labor a great labor' (Ezek 29:18), *va-yaʿavidu Miṣrayim* 'and the Egyptians made [them] labor' (Exod 1:13), *maʿavidim otam* 'making them labor' (Exod 6:5). [So] *va-ʿavadum* is not from these two patterns, but rather from what is non-transitive³, like *va-ʿavado le-ʿolam* 'and he shall serve him forever' (Exod 21:6). End. — And it is not admissible that the duration of the being-employed and the being-afflicted should be 400 years, since they did n[ot] dwell in E[gy]pt for 400 years; rather their dwelling in it was 210 years, of which the totality of the affliction was about 80 years from the time of the [birth and] life of the messenger⁴ (peace be upon him). And the start of these 400 ye[ar]s is the year of the birth of Isaac. Do you not see that Jacob was born to him [Isaac] [w]hen he was 60 years of age, as in his saying *ve-Yiṣḥaq ben shishshim shana be-ledet otam* 'and Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them' (Gen 25:26); and the age of Jacob at his entry into Egypt was 130 years, as in his saying to Pharaoh *yemei shenei megurai sheloshim u-meʾat shana* 'the days of the years of my sojournings are 130 years' (Gen 47:9). So the total becomes [1]90 years; there remain from the 400, two hundred and ten years — and this is the duration of their dwelling in Egypt. End.
content.comments: ¹ yastakhdimūhum (يستخدمونهم) — "they shall employ them [as servants]"; the form-X Arabic verb of kh-d-m, taking a direct object. ² mutaʿaddī (متعدٍّ) — "transitive, [verb that] passes [its action onto an object]"; the Arabic-grammar term, applied here to Hebrew morphology. ³ ghayr mutaʿaddī (غير متعدٍّ) — "non-transitive, intransitive"; the standard antonym. Ali's grammatical point: va-ʿavadum cannot mean 'they made them serve' (transitive), but means 'they served them' (intransitive with a dative object) — and accordingly the affliction (ve-ʿinnu otam) is a separate predicate. ⁴ al-rasūl (الرسول) — "the messenger"; Ali's standard designation for Moses in his Karaite tafsīr register, drawing on the Qurʾānic/kalām usage.

content.hebrew: Gen 17:9
content.english: Gen 17:9

content.hebrew: ויאמר יי אל אברהם ואתה את בריתי תשמור –
content.english: **"And the LORD said to Abraham: as for you, you shall keep my covenant"** (*va-yomer YY el Avraham ve-attah et beriti tishmor*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion picks up at himol lakhem in the next verse.

content.hebrew: – קולה המול [ל]כם כל זכר – הו מצדר במתׄל אלאמר יעני אכׄתתאן יכׄתן כל [דׄ]כר לכם ודׄלך מכׄצוץ בגיר מחגׄוגׄ ואמא אלמחגׄוגׄ [פי]לזמה אן יכׄ[תן] נפסה מן קולה וערל [ז]כר (בראשית יז:יד) למא תצׄמנה מן אלועיד.
content.english: His saying **"there shall be circumcised among [yo]u every male"** (*himol [la]khem kol zakhar*). It is an infinitive¹ in the manner of the imperative — meaning: let there be a circumcising performed on every [m]ale among you. And this is restricted² to one not yet [bound by] the [revealed] proof³; as for the one [bound by] the proof, it is incumbent upon him that he c[ircumcise] himself — [as appears] from his saying *ve-ʿarel [za]khar* 'and an uncircumcised [m]ale' (Gen 17:14), in view of the [punitive] threat it contains.
content.comments: ¹ maṣdar (مصدر) — "infinitive, [verbal] noun"; the Arabic-grammar term, applied here to the Hebrew infinitive absolute himmol used in imperative force. ² makhṣūṣ (مخصوص) — "restricted, [the object of] specification"; the uṣūl al-fiqh term for what has had takhṣīṣ applied to it. ³ al-maḥjūj (المحجوج) — "the [one bound by] the [revealed] proof, [the one] against whom the [scriptural] argument stands"; the kalām designation for the adult subject of taklīf. Ali's two-fold division: the eight-day-old child is circumcised by the agency of his father, since he himself is not yet a subject of religious obligation; the adult male, by contrast, is personally responsible for his own circumcision.

content.hebrew: ונמלתם –
content.english: **"And you shall be circumcised"** (*u-nemaltem*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion begins at besar ʿorlatekhem.

content.hebrew: – קולה בשר ערלתכם – הו תעריף אלשי אלמקטוע מן [חי]תׄ כאן קולה המול לכם (בראשית יז:י) לא יערף מנה דׄלך. אדׄ אלקריב [אן] אלכׄתאנה̈ לם תערף אלא מן זמאן אברהם ואלמגׄר. ואצׄאף אלבשר אלי אלערלה מן חיתׄ כא[נ]ת וצפא פיה אדׄ ליס כל בשר ערל כמא אן זהב המנורה מצׄאף אלי וצף פיה והו אלשכל אלדׄי [צא]ר [ב]ה אלדׄהב מנארה̈ וליס כל דׄהב מנארה̈ כ[מ]א אן ליס כל לחם מן לחם אלאנסאן יסמי ערלה. בל אלערלה וצף לה יתמיז בהא מן לחם גירהא וקד קיל אן בשר ע[ר]לתכם הו אלאחליל אדׄ יסמי בשר כק׳ זב מבשרו (ויקרא טו:ב) ואלערלה הי עלי ראסה פאמר בקטעהא ואצׄאף אלבשר אליהא תמייזא לה מן סאיר אעצׄא אלאנסאן פחצל הדׄא אלעצׄו אלדׄי הו בשר יסמי פי אל[ע]בראני נמול ופי אלערבי מכׄתונא לאגׄל דׄלך.
content.english: His saying **"the flesh of your foreskin"** (*besar ʿorlatkhem*). This is the identification of the thing to be cut, since His saying *himol lakhem* 'circumcise [every male] for yourselves' (Gen 17:10) does not [suffice to] make that known — as it is plausible that circumcision was not known until the time of Abraham and after. And he annexed *basar* 'flesh' to *ʿorlah* 'foreskin' because the [foreskin] is a descriptive qualifier¹ in it [the flesh], since not all flesh is uncircumcised — just as *zahav ha-menorah* 'the gold of the lampstand' is annexed to a descriptive qualifier in it [the gold], namely the form that the gold [com]es to take, [the lampstand-shape]; and not every gold [piece] is a lampstand. Likewise not every flesh of the human is called *ʿorlah*; rather *ʿorlah* is a descriptive qualifier distinguishing it from other flesh. And it has been said that *besar ʿo[r]latekhem* refers to the male organ², since it is called *basar*, as in [the verse] *zav mi-besaro* 'one who has a discharge from his flesh' (Lev 15:2); and the *ʿorlah* is upon its head, and he commanded the cutting of it; and he annexed *basar* to it as a distinguishing marker from the other organs of the human. So this organ, which is *basar*, is called in [H]ebrew *namul* and in Arabic *makhtūn*, on account of that.
content.comments: ¹ waṣf (وصف) — "descriptive qualifier, [restrictive] attribute"; the Arabic-grammar term for a qualifying annexation that distinguishes one species from a broader genus. ² al-iḥlīl (الإحليل) — "the male [generative] organ"; the standard Arabic anatomical term, used here in the tradition's polite circumlocutionary register.

content.hebrew: וקולה לאות ברית – יעני אן הדׄה אלכׄתאנה̈ הי עלאמה̈ ללעהד אלדׄי ביני ובינכם (בראשית יז:יא) מן חיתׄ אדׄא ראוכם אלמכׄאלפין מיזוכם ממן ליס פיה דׄלך כמא ימיזוכם בחפטׄ אלסבת אלמקול פיהא כי אות היא ביני וביניכם (שמות לא:יג). פאלמילה הי אות ואלברית הו א[לא]מר בהא.
content.english: And his saying **"for a sign of [the] covenant"** (*le-ot berit*). It means: that this circumcision is a sign for the covenant *beini u-veneikhem* 'between me and you' (Gen 17:11), in that when the religious opposers¹ see you, they will distinguish you from those in whom that [sign] is not [present] — just as they distinguish you by your keeping of the Sabbath, of which it is said *ki ot hi beini u-veneikhem* 'for it is a sign between me and you' (Exod 31:13). For the *millah* [the act of circumcision] is the sign, and the *berit* [covenant] is the command for it.
content.comments: ¹ al-mukhālifīn (المخالفين) — "the [religious] opposers, [those who] dissent"; the Karaite kalām designation for adherents of other religions and schools — here, in the Sabbath-and-circumcision context, primarily the Muslims and Christians among whom the Karaite community lived.

content.hebrew: ובן שמנת ימים – קד יטלק עלי [מ]ן לה תׄמניה̈ איאם כאמלה̈ אבן תׄמניה̈ איאם ויטלק איצׄא
content.english: **"And at eight days old"** (*u-ven shemonat yamim*). This expression is sometimes applied to one for whom eight days are complete, [calling him] *ibn thamāniyat ayyām* 'eight days old'; and it is applied also…

content.hebrew: ה[דׄא] אלאסם עלי מן לם תכמל לה בחיתׄ תכון נאקצה̈ אלטרפין או אחדהמא פאלחקיקה̈ פי דׄלך כון אלתׄמניה̈ כאמלה̈ [פ]אן כאן אברהם קד דל עלי אנה אן כאן אולהא וא[כׄ]רהא נאקצא פעל אלפרץׄ פי אלתׄאמן פדׄלך גׄאיז ואלא פאלאולי אדׄא ולד לה אלמולוד מתׄלא יום אלאתׄנין אלטׄהר אן יכׄת[נ]ה יום אלתׄלתׄא אלטׄהר ליכון אלתׄמניה̈ איאם כא[מלה̈] ונחן קד גנינא ען דׄל[ך] בקול אלרסול עליה אלסלם וביום השמיני ימול (ויקרא יב:ג) לאן דׄלך ינבגי אלכׄתאנה̈ פי אליום אלתׄאמן ל[למ]ולוד נאקצא כאן אם כאמלא.
content.english: …[t]his [same] designation to one for whom they are not complete — such that the two endpoints, or one of them, are deficient. The literal sense¹ in this is the completeness of the eight; [so] if Abraham (peace be upon him) had indicated that — were its first and its [la]st [day] deficient — the discharge of the obligation² on the eighth would [still] be valid, that would be admissible; but otherwise, the better course is that, when the newborn is born to him on, say, a clear Monday, he should circumci[s]e him on a clear Tuesday [the following week], so that the eight days may be com[plete]. And we have been spared³ from [needing to settle] th[is question] by the messenger's saying (peace be upon him) *u-va-yom ha-shemini yimmol* 'and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised' (Lev 12:3), since that requires that the circumcision be on the eighth day for the [new]born, deficient [in its end-days] or complete.
content.comments: ¹ al-ḥaqīqa (الحقيقة) — "the literal sense, [the] primary [meaning]"; see Gen 12:1 footnote. ² al-farḍ (الفرض) — "the [scripturally] obligatory, the obligation"; the legal category, near-synonym of al-wājib. ³ ghuninā (غُنينا) — "we have been spared, [we have been] dispensed [from needing to settle this]"; the Mosaic specification, on Ali's reading, settles what would otherwise be a vexed question about counting endpoints.

content.hebrew: – וקולה י[מול] – י[גׄ]וז כון אלנון מנ[ה] מכׄתצרה̈ ותקדירה ינמול מתׄל יקום (דברים לב:מג) אלדׄי תקדי[רה] ינקום [ו]מענאה יכׄתן אלכׄתאן ויגׄוז כונה ממא ליס אצלה נון מן הדׄה אללגה̈ והו גיר מתעדי מתׄל יכון (משלי יב:ג) אלדׄי אמרה הכון לקראת אלהיך (עמוס ד:יב) וכק׳ המול ימול יליד ביתך (בראשית יז:יג).
content.english: And his saying **"he shall be circumcised"** (*yimmol*). It is [ad]missible that the *nun* in [it] be elided¹, its supplied reading being *yinnamol* — like *yaqom* (Deut 32:43), whose supplied reading is *yinnaqom*; and its meaning is 'he shall be circumcised' (the passive). And it is admissible that it be [a form] whose root has no *nun* in this verbal class, in which case it is non-transitive — like *yikkon* 'shall be established' (Prov 12:3), whose imperative is *hikkon liqraʾt Elohekha* 'be prepared to meet your God' (Amos 4:12), and as in [the verse] *himmol yimmol yelid beithekha* 'the homeborn shall surely be circumcised' (Gen 17:13).
content.comments: ¹ mukhtaṣara (مختصرة) — "elided, [morphologically] contracted"; the standard Arabic-grammar designation for a letter dropped under specific morphological conditions. Ali's grammatical analysis: yimmol can be parsed either as a niphal of m-w-l with the prefix-nun assimilated (yinnamol), or as a qal of a hollow root, intransitive.

content.hebrew: – וקולה כל זכר – בעד קולה ובן שמונת ימים (בראשית יז:יב) לתרפע אשכאל פי באב אלאנתׄי אדׄ לפטׄ בן יקע עליהא כק׳ בעצב תלדי בנים (בראשית ג:טז).
content.english: And his saying **"every male"** (*kol zakhar*) — [coming] after his saying *u-ven shemonat yamim* 'and at eight days old' (Gen 17:12) — [is] to remove an ambiguity in the matter of the female, since the term *ben* may fall upon her, as in [the verse] *be-ʿetsev teledi vanim* 'in pain you shall bear children' (Gen 3:16).

content.hebrew: – וקולה יליד בית – ואו אלעטף מחדׄופה̈ מנה לאן לכם אקתצׄי אולאדכם וקתדירה ויליד בית יעני ולד אלעבד ואלאמה̈ אלמתואלד פי מנאזלהם.
content.english: And his saying **"a homeborn slave"** (*yelid bayit*). The conjunctive vav¹ is elided from it, since *lakhem* 'for you' [above] required ['your] sons' [as the prior subject]; the supplied reading is *vi-yelid bayit* 'and a homeborn slave' — meaning the child of the male slave and the female slave, born within their dwellings.
content.comments: ¹ wāw al-ʿaṭf (واو العطف) — "the vav of conjunction"; see Gen 9 seg. 222 footnote.

content.hebrew: – וקולה ומקנת כסף – יעני אלעבד אלמשתרי באלתׄמן ואל[מ]עארץׄ בה ומן יחצל מן אלעביד משביא או הדיה̈ קד יקאס עלי מקנת כסף לכונה אכתׄר פי אלממאליך.
content.english: And his saying **"and one acquired with money"** (*u-miqnat kesef*). It means: the slave purchased with the price, and the one [b]artered for it; and slaves who come [into one's possession] as captives or as a gift are extended by analogy¹ to [the category of] *miqnat kesef* — since this [purchase-by-price] is the predominant [mode] in slave-ownership.
content.comments: ¹ qiyās (قياس) — "analogy, [legal] inference by parallel"; the uṣūl al-fiqh term for the extension of a ruling from a stated case to an unstated case sharing the same ʿilla. The Karaites accept qiyās as a legitimate juridical method, against the Rabbanite thirteen middot.

content.hebrew: – וקולה מכל בן נכר יעם סאיר מן כׄרגׄ ען זרע [א]ברהם.
content.english: And his saying **"from every son of a foreigner"** (*mi-kol ben nekhar*) takes in everyone who is outside the seed of [A]braham.

content.hebrew: – וקולה אשר לא מזרעך הוא קיל אנה [ו]צף לבן נכר (בראשית יז:יב) לתרפע שבהה̈ עסאהא תחצל פי אולאד אקארב אברהם באן יקאל ליס הם גרבא ענה פמנע מן דׄלך בקולה אשר לא [מז]רעך הוא (בראשית יז:יב) לידכׄל פי דׄלך אלגיר ממן ליס במדכור ודׄלך [כׄאר]גׄ אלי דלאלה̈.
content.english: And his saying **"who is not of your seed"** (*asher lo mi-zarʿakha hu*). It is said: that this is a [q]ualifier¹ for *ben nekhar* 'a foreigner's son' (Gen 17:12), to remove a possible [confusion]² [regarding] the children of Abraham's relatives, [where one] might say they are not foreigners to him; so he forbids that by his saying *asher lo [mi-z]arʿakha hu* 'who is not of your seed' (Gen 17:12), so that there may enter into [the obligation also] the others not [explicitly] mentioned — and that [extension] comes out as a [conventional] indication³.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. waṣf. ² See glossary s.v. shubha. ³ See glossary s.v. dalāla.

content.hebrew: – המול ימו[ל]
content.english: **"He shall surely be circumcised"** (*himmol yimmo[l]*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; gloss picks up at the second mention of yelid beithekha u-miqnat kaspekha.

content.hebrew: – קולה תׄאניא יליד ביתך ומקנת כספך – קיל י[ע]ני בה מן כאן מנהמא לה אזיד מן תׄ[מ]ניה̈ איאם לולאדתה פאוגׄב כׄתנה איצׄא אדׄ כאן הדׄא גיר [מ]סתפאד ממא תק[דם].
content.english: His [s]aying — for a second time¹ — **"the homeborn of your house and the one acquired with your money"** (*yelid beithekha u-miqnat kaspekha*). It is said: he m[e]ans by it the one of these two for whom more than e[i]ght days from his birth have already passed; so he obligated his circumcision also, since this was not [d]erived from what came [before].
content.comments: ¹ thāniyan (ثانياً) — "a second time, [in a] repeated [mention]"; the uṣūl/hermeneutical term for a scriptural repetition whose redundancy must be cashed out by supplying it with a new juridical purchase.

content.hebrew: – וקולה והיתה בריתי בבש׳ – יעני בה [ע]לא[מ]ה̈ [אל]עהד עלי מא מצׄי פי לאות ברית
content.english: And his saying **"and my covenant shall be in your flesh"** (*ve-hayetah beriti bi-vesar[khem]*). He means by it the [s]i[g]n of the [c]ovenant, on the basis of what was settled in *le-ot berit* 'for a sign of the covenant' [above].

content.hebrew: – וקולה לברית עולם – אפאד אלתאביד פי הדׄא אלברית
content.english: And his saying **"for an everlasting covenant"** (*li-vrit ʿolam*). It conveys¹ the perpetuity² of this covenant.
content.comments: ¹ afāda (أفاد) — "conveys, [imparts a juridical] consequence"; the uṣūl term for the legal force a scriptural expression brings. ² al-taʾbīd (التأبيد) — "perpetuity, [perdurance without temporal limit]"; the uṣūl al-fiqh term for the unlimited temporal scope of a ruling — over against al-tawqīt (a stipulated term).

content.hebrew: – וערל זכר – דׄלך יתנאול אלבאלג מן ולד אברהם עליה אלסלם ואלדכׄיל פי אלדין עלי ראי מן ירי אן אשר לא מזרעך הוא (בראשית יז:יב) יקתצׄי [5]דלך באכׄתצאר ואו ועלי ראי מן לם ירי דׄלך יקול הו מכׄצוץ באלבאלג מן ו[ל]ד אברהם ומן יתגׄה הדׄא אלתכליף אליה סואהם מן יליד בית ומקנת כסף (בראשית יז:יב) פאמא מן לם יתגׄה הדׄא אלתכליף אליה פליס הו מעניא בדׄלך מתׄל שם ולוט וגירהמא.
content.english: **"And an uncircumcised male"** (*ve-ʿarel zakhar*). This takes in the [physically] adult¹ male of the descendants of Abraham (peace be upon him) and the convert², according to the view of those who hold that *asher lo mi-zarʿakha hu* 'who is not of your seed' (Gen 17:12) requires [the conversion case] by the elision of a vav; and according to the view of those who do not hold that, [the verse here] is restricted to the adult male of the desce[n]dants of Abraham and to those [others] upon whom this moral obligation is directed apart from them — [namely,] from [the category of] *yelid bayit u-miqnat kesef* 'the homeborn and the one bought with money' (Gen 17:12). As for one upon whom this obligation is not directed, he is not the [intended] referent of [the verse] — like Shem and Lot and others.
content.comments: ¹ al-bāligh (البالغ) — "the [physically] adult, [the one who has] attained [maturity]"; the legal term for the physiologically mature subject capable of taklīf. ² al-dakhīl fī l-dīn (الدخيل في الدين) — "the convert, [the one who has] entered into the [religious] community"; the standard Arabic legal-religious term, neutral between Jewish, Christian, and Islamic usage.

content.hebrew: – וקולה ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מעמיה – וקיל מענאה אלתברי ואלאנפצאל מנה ואן לא יכׄאלט
content.english: And his saying **"and that soul shall be cut off from its people"** (*ve-nikhretah ha-nefesh ha-hi mei-ʿammeha*). And some have said: its meaning is the disowning¹ [of him by the community] and the separation from him, and that he should not mingle…
content.comments: ¹ al-tabarrī (التبرّي) — "disowning, [public] repudiation"; the social-juridical act by which the community publicly distances itself from the deviant — construed here as the cashing-out of *karet* in the communal rather than the metaphysical sense.

content.hebrew: ויגׄתמע בה ודׄלך יקתצׄי כון אלאכׄלאל בדׄלך כבירא
content.english: …with him or assemble with him; and that requires that the breach in this [commandment] be [reckoned as] a grave [offense]¹.
content.comments: ¹ kabīr (كبير) — "[a] grave [offense]"; the standard Qurʾānic/kalām category of the major sin, drawing the weightiest sanctions.

content.hebrew: – וקולה את בריתי הפר – יגׄרי [מ]גׄרי אלתעליל יעני ונכרתה הנפש ההיא מע[מ]יה (בראשית יז:יד) לאנה בריתי הפר והו בוז[ן] הקל (ישעיהו ח:כה) פעל מאצׄי וא[מ]רה הפר בוזן השב אל תער[ה] (יחזקאל כא:לה) השע ממני (תהלים לט:יד) ה
content.english: And his saying **"he has broken my covenant"** (*et beriti hefar*). It runs the [c]ourse of providing the rationale¹ — meaning: *ve-nikhretah ha-nefesh ha-hi mei-ʿa[mm]eha* 'and that soul shall be cut off from its people' (Gen 17:14) on account of [the fact that] *beriti hefar* 'he broke my covenant.' And it is on the measur[e] of *heqal* (Isa 8:25) — a past-tense verb — and its imperative² is *hafer* on the measure of *hashev el taʿa[reha]* 'return [the sword] to [its] she[ath]' (Ezek 21:35), [or] *hashaʿ mimmenni* 'look away from me' (Ps 39:14). End.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taʿlīl. ² amr (أمر) — "imperative"; Arabic-grammar term, applied here to Hebrew morphology.

content.hebrew: Gen 18:1
content.english: Gen 18:1

content.hebrew: וירא אליו ייי באלוני ממרא –
content.english: **"And the LORD appeared to him at the oaks of Mamre"** (*va-yera elav YY be-Eloney Mamre*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion jumps to vv. 17–19.

content.hebrew: וייי אמר המכסה אני (בראשית יח:יז). ו[אבר]הם היו יהי[ה] (בראשית יח:יח). כי ידעתיו (בראשית יח:יט). אלאקרב כון אברהם גיר מכׄא[ט]ב בהדׄה אלג׳ פואסיק אדׄ ליס מצׄמונהא כׄטאבא מעה ומקאבלה̈ לה בל לגירה אכׄבארא בעטׄם מנזלתה ענד אללה תעאלי ואלקריב כון דׄלך תעריפא במנזלה̈ אברהם למשה עליה אלסלם ואמר בתדוינה פי אלתורה לכנה לא בד מן כון דׄלך או[ל]א כׄטאבא מן אללה עז וגׄל למכׄאטב מא אמא מלך או גירה תׄם אכׄבר בה משה ודונה כאכׄבארה במא סואה ממא תצׄמנתה שריעתה מן חיתׄ אן קולה ויי אמר טׄאהרה ידל עלי כׄטאב וקע מנה תעאלי במא ורד מן הדׄה אלנצוץ. ולא יחסן דׄלך מן דון מכׄאטב יסמע ויפהם למא לה פיה מן אלצלאח ליכׄרגׄ כׄטאבה עז וגׄל בדׄלך מן כונה עבתׄא ואלא י[גׄר]י מגׄרי מכׄאטבה̈ אלגׄמאד וגירה ממא לא יגׄוז עליה סבחאנה ויגׄוז [מע] דׄלך כון אברהם עליה אלסלם קד ערף בוקוע הדׄא אלכׄטאב מנה סבחאנה למן כׄאטב בה אן כ[א]ן לה פי הדׄא אלתע[ר]יף צלאח ולא...א לה אנא ממא יסרה.
content.english: *ve-YY amar ha-mekhasseh ani* 'and the LORD said: shall I hide…' (Gen 18:17); *ve-[Avra]ham hayo yihy[eh]* 'and [Abra]ham shall surely become…' (Gen 18:18); *ki yedaʿtiv* 'for I have known him' (Gen 18:19). The most plausible¹ [view] is that Abraham was not the add[r]essee of these three pericopes — since their substance is not an address to him and a confrontation of him, but rather, an [address] to another, reporting of the greatness of his standing with God (may He be exalted). And it is plausible that this is a making-known of the standing of Abraham to Moses (peace be upon him), and a command to him to record it in the Torah. But it must be that this is in the first [i]nstance an address from God (mighty and majestic) to some [other] addressee — be it an angel or another — and then Moses was informed of it and recorded it, [just] as [he was informed of] his other [reports] from what his law contains; inasmuch as His saying *ve-YY amar* 'and the LORD said' — its apparent sense — indicates that an address occurred from Him (may He be exalted) by what came forth of these utterances. And that [act of address] is not [theologically] good apart from there being an addressee who hears and understands — [an addressee] for whom there is welfare² in it — so as to exclude His (mighty and majestic) address by it from being pointless³, lest [it pro]ceed in the manner of address to inanimate matter and the like, [a thing] which is not admissible upon Him (praise be to Him). And it is admissible [along with that] that Abraham (peace be upon him) was informed of the occurrence of this address from Him (praise be to Him) to the one He addressed by it — provided that there [w]ere [some] welfare for him in this notification, and not […] for him, [in] what would give him joy.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. al-aqrab. ² ṣalāḥ (صلاح) — "welfare"; see Gen 6:6 footnote. Ali's theological constraint: divine speech, like any rational action, must be directed to an end conducing to some agent's welfare; otherwise it is ʿabath (pointless), which is incompatible with divine wisdom. ³ ʿabath (عبث) — "pointless [action], purposeless"; the kalām category of an act lacking any rational end, excluded from God's conduct by all Karaite/Muʿtazilite theology.

content.hebrew: וק[ו]לה המכסה אני מא׳ – [טׄא]הרה אלאסתפהאם מתׄל המקנא אתה לי (במדבר יא:כט) ולמא לם
content.english: And his s[ay]ing **"shall I hide…"** (*ha-mekhasseh ani*). Its [appa]rent sense is interrogation, like *ha-meqanne attah li* 'are you jealous for me?' (Num 11:29). And since…

content.hebrew: יגׄז על[י]ה תעאלי אלאסתפהאם כאן [מ]עני דׄלך אלנפי מע כון טׄא[ה]רה אתׄבאתא פכאנה תעאל[י] קאל לא אגטי ען אברהם מא אנא פא[ע]לה בל אכ[ש]פה לה מן חיתׄ אנה סיכון מנה חזבא עטׄימא ומן חיתׄ אני נאגׄיתה במא יוצי בה בניה ואלה מן בעדה מן חפטׄ טאעתי ותמאמה. ולין כאן יגׄרי דׄלך מגׄרי אחדנא ממן לא ירי אכׄפא סרה עמן יודה ויואליה פאן אלקדים עז וגׄל מע מחבתה לאברהם לו לם יחצל פי כשף לה מא יריד בנזלה מן אלבלא באהל סדום ג[ר]ץׄ יכׄץ אלתכליף למא כשפה. אלא תרי אלי מא טׄהר מן כׄצׄו[ע]ה פי סואלה ואסתדפאעה בסבב אהל סדום ומנאזלתה [ל]ה עז וגׄל פי עדד אלצאלחין מנהם אלי עדד אלקליל לם יסתחסן בעדה אלאסתחטאט ענה. ואלגרץׄ בקולה כי לא יעשה יי אלהים דבר כי אם גלה סודו אל עבדיו הנביאים (עמוס ג:ז) גׄאר הדׄא אלמגׄרי פי אן אלדׄי יכשפה מן אסרארה תע[אל]י אלי אנביאיה הו מא יקתצׄי אלצלאח כשפה אליהם פמא אכתׄר מא יפעל תעאלי ממא לא יעלם בה אלא בוד חדותׄה.
content.english: …interrogation is not admissible upon Him (may He be exalted), the [m]eaning of that is the negative, while its appa[r]ent sense is the [affirmative]¹: as though He (may He be exalt[ed]) had said: 'I do not conceal from Abraham what I am do[i]ng; rather, I r[ev]eal it to him' — inasmuch as he will [in time] become a great nation, and inasmuch as I have entrusted to him in confidence what he will enjoin upon his sons and his house after him, of the keeping of My obedience and [its] completeness. And although that runs the course of [the conduct of] one of us who does not [think it right] to hide his secret from the one who loves him and stands close — yet the Eternal (mighty and majestic), along with His love for Abraham, [would] not [have made this revelation] had not, in His revealing to him what He intended to bring down upon the people of Sodom of the calamity, been some pu[r]pose specific to taklīf — for that He revealed [it]. Do you not see what manifested of his submi[ssi]on² in his asking and interceding on behalf of the people of Sodom, and his haggl[ing] with [Him] (mighty and majestic) over the number of the righteous among them down to a small number, [after which] he no longer thought it fitting to lower [it] further? And the purpose of his saying *ki lo yaʿaseh YY Elohim davar ki im galah sodo el ʿavadav ha-neviʾim* 'for the Lord GOD does no matter except that He reveals his secret to His servants the prophets' (Amos 3:7) runs in this manner: that what He reveals of His secrets (may He be ex[al]ted) to his prophets is what welfare requires Him to reveal to them — and how much, indeed, [does] He (may He be exalted) do that one knows of only at the moment of its coming to be.
content.comments: ¹ ithbāt (إثبات) — "the affirmative, [the] positive [predication]"; the standard logical/grammatical antonym of nafy (negation). Ali's interpretive move: interrogation in divine speech is rhetorical and carries negative force ("shall I hide?" = "I will not hide"). ² khuḍūʿ (خضوع) — "submission, [reverent] lowliness"; the kalām/devotional category for the inward disposition of the petitioner before God.

content.hebrew: וקולה ונברכו בו – אמא אן יריד באברהם ואמא נסלה אלדׄין ה[ם] גוי גדול ועצום (בראשית יח:יח) כק׳ ליעקב ונברכו בך כל משפחות [ה]אדמה ובזרעך (בראשית כח:יד).
content.english: And his saying **"and shall be blessed in him"** (*ve-nivrekhu vo*). Either he intends Abraham [himself], or [he intends] his offspring who [a]re *goy gadol ve-ʿaṣum* 'a great and mighty nation' (Gen 18:18) — as in [the verse] to Jacob *ve-nivrekhu vekha kol mishpeḥot [ha-]adamah u-ve-zarʿakha* 'and through you shall be blessed all the families of [the] earth, and through your seed' (Gen 28:14).

content.hebrew: וקולה כי ידעתיו – יפסר מן [א]ל[מ]נאגׄאה̈ מתׄל אשר ידעו [יי] פנים אל פנים (דברים לד:י). ו[מ]עני אלמנאגׄאה̈ הו אלמכׄאטבה̈ עלי וגׄה אלאגׄלאל. וקד יכון דׄלך בגיר ואסטה̈ ככׄטאבה למוס[י] עליה אלסלם
content.english: And his saying **"for I have known him"** (*ki yedaʿtiv*). It is interpreted from [the sense of] [i]ntim[ate communion]¹, like *asher yedaʿo [YY] panim el panim* 'whom [the LORD] knew face to face' (Deut 34:10). And the [m]eaning of intimate communion² is the addressing [of someone] in the manner of honoring. And this is sometimes without an intermediary, as in His addressing of Mos[es] (peace be upon him)…
content.comments: ¹ al-munājāh (المناجاة) — "intimate [private] communion, [the] whispered colloquy"; the kalām/devotional term for direct, unmediated communication between God and the intimate servant, paradigmatically Moses on Sinai. ² Same term repeated; Ali reads Hebrew yedaʿtiv as denoting this elevated mode of address.

content.hebrew: ויגׄוז כון אברהם קד [כׄו]טב עלי הדׄ[א א]לחד בבעץׄ אלפרא[יץׄ] אלמכׄתצה̈ בה ובאלה. וליס קולה ולא [ק]ם נביא ע[ו]ד כמשה וג׳ (דברים לד:י) מענאה מן דׄלך אדׄ ליס אברהם מבעו[תׄ]א פי ישראל ולאן טׄאהר דׄלך אלאסתקבאל ה
content.english: …and it is admissible that Abraham was [ad]dressed on th[is] standard with some of the [legal] obliga[tions] specific to him and his household. And his [Moses's] saying *ve-lo [qa]m navi ʿ[o]d ke-Moshe* 'and there [ar]ose no [other] prophet [li]ke Moses' etc. (Deut 34:10) does not bear that meaning — since Abraham was not [d]ispatched as a [prophet] in [the people of] Israel; and [moreover] because the surface sense of [Deut 34:10] is about [the] future¹. End.
content.comments: ¹ al-istiqbāl (الاستقبال) — "the future"; see Gen 11:9 footnote. Ali's argument: Deut 34:10 is a prospective comparison (Moses' supremacy among future Israelite prophets), so it does not exclude the patriarchs from having received direct address.

content.hebrew: חלילה לך מעשות כדבר הזה – אלדׄי נזה אברהם אללה סבחאנה ענה הו אהלאך אלצדיק ואלרשע עלי חד סוא כק׳ והיה כצדיק כרשע (בראשית יח:כה) פאמא אמאתתהמא גׄמיעא באפה̈ ואחדה̈ פמא נזהה עז ו[גׄ]ל ענה לגׄואז דׄלך. לכן אלפרק בינהמא הו [א]ן מא ינזל באל[ר]שע מן אלאפה̈ יכון עקובה̈ לה ילקא פעלה ומא ינזל ב[אל]צדיק מן דׄלך הו מחנה̈ לה יסתחק עליה אלאגׄר ואלעוץׄ פבאלקצד יתמיז אלצׄרר אלנאזל באלצדיק מן אלצׄרר א[ל]נאזל באלרשע מע אתפאקהמא פי אלצׄרר ואדׄא כאן כדׄלך. פיקרב כון גרצׄה עליה אלסלם במא נזהה ענה מן הדׄא אלבאב צׄרבא מן אלתשפע יעני אן כאן יסוג פי אלחכמה̈ אמהאל אהל סדום לאגׄל [כון] בינהם מן אלצלחא פמא אולאך בה ואן כנת אעלם אנך לו אהלכת אלגׄמיע לכאן עדלא מנך לאני אעלם אנך לא תמית אל[צ]דיק כאמאתה̈ אלרשע אלתי הי עקובה̈ לה חאשאך מן הדׄא לאן מן הו חאכם [גׄמי]ע אהל אלארץׄ באלעדל לא יפעל ה[דׄ]א אלחכם לכנה יא רב אן כאנת [א]מאתתהמא מעא תסוג פי חכ[מ]ך. פקד יחסן איצׄא תמייז אל[צ]דיק מן אלאפה̈ אלנאזלה̈ באל[ר]שע לתקוי רגבה̈ אלנאס פי [אל]צדקות ו[ל]א י[גׄרי] בהמא [מ]גׄרי ואחדא פיצׄעף יקינהם פי אלדין [ו]א[ן] כא[נ]וא ענד דׄלך מותאיין מן קבל אנפסהם פגׄאה אלגׄואב אני לא אהלכהם אן כאן פיהם מן אלצדיקים אלעדד אלמדׄכור כק׳ ויא׳ יי אם אמצא בסדום חמשים צדיקים וג׳ (בראשית יח:כו) ה
content.english: **"Far be it from you to do a thing like this!"** (*ḥalilah lekha mei-ʿasot ka-davar ha-zeh*). What Abraham [held God] above (*nazzaha*)¹ is the destroying of the righteous and the wicked on a single standard, as in [the verse] *ve-haya ka-ṣaddiq ka-rashaʿ* 'and the righteous would be as the wicked' (Gen 18:25). But as for the [mere] putting both of them to death by a single calamity — that he did not declare God free of, given the admissibility of that. Rather, the difference between them is that what comes down upon the [w]icked of calamity is a penalty for him; he meets [the consequence of] his deed. And what comes down upon [the] righteous of that is a trial² for him, by which he earns reward and compensation³. So by [divine] intent⁴ the harm coming down upon the righteous is distinguished from the harm c[o]ming down upon the wicked, despite their convergence in the [outward] harm. — And since that is so, it is plausible that [Abraham's] (peace be upon him) purpose, in what he [held God] free of in this respect, is a kind of intercession⁵ — meaning: 'if it is admissible in [Your] wisdom that You should grant a reprieve to the people of Sodom on account of [the presence] among them of [some] righteous, then how more so [should You], [even] though I know that were You to destroy all, that would be justice from You — for I know that You do not put the [r]ighteous to death as You put the wicked to death (a penalty for him); far be it from You from this, for the One who is judge of [a]ll the people of the earth in justice does not give th[a]t ruling. But, O Lord, if their being put to death together would be admissible in Your wis[do]m, [then] the distinguishing of the [r]ighteous from the calamity coming down upon the [w]icked may also be [deemed] good, so as to strengthen the people's yearning for [the] virtues, and so that the [t]wo not [pro]ceed for them in [a] single manner — which would weaken their certainty in religion, [e]ven though they [the righteous] in that [event] would [have been] dying anyway, from their own [natural causes]'. And [suddenly] came the response: 'I will not destroy them, if there be among them of the righteous the number mentioned,' as in [the verse] *va-yo[mer] YY im emṣa vi-Sdom ḥamishshim ṣaddiqim* 'and the LORD said: if I find in Sodom fifty righteous' etc. (Gen 18:26). End.
content.comments: ¹ nazzaha (نزَّه) — "to hold above, [theologically] declare-free-of"; the kalām form-II verb, the central act of negative theology, by which a quality is declared inadmissible of the divine essence. ² miḥna (محنة) — "trial, [test by] suffering"; the kalām theodicy category for divinely sent suffering that does not penalize but rather furnishes occasion for the agent's earning of reward. ³ al-ajr wa-l-ʿiwaḍ (الأجر والعوض) — "reward and compensation"; the standard Muʿtazilite pair: ajr for obedience, ʿiwaḍ for undeserved suffering. The doctrine of ʿiwaḍ is central to Muʿtazilite/Karaite theodicy. ⁴ al-qaṣd (القصد) — "[divine] intent, [the] aim"; the kalām category that distinguishes acts whose outward form coincides but whose ethical value differs by the agent's intent. ⁵ al-tashaffuʿ (التشفع) — "intercession, [pleading on behalf of another]"; the kalām/devotional term for the suppliant's intervention with God for others.

content.hebrew: יתוגׄה פי קצה̈ אבימלך פי אכׄדׄה לשרה [מ]סאיל: והי כיף חסן תהדיד אבימלך ומעאקבתה מן גׄהה̈ [ש]רה מע אעתדׄארה מן דׄלך בולה בתם לבבי ובנקיון כפי עשיתי זאת (בראשית כ:ה) ותצדיקה לה פי דׄלך בקולה
content.english: There arises in the story of Abimelech in his taking of Sarah [several] [q]uestions¹: namely, how is it good [for God] to threaten Abimelech and to penalize him with respect to [S]arah, alongside his apology² for that in his saying *be-tom levavi u-ve-niqyon kappay ʿasiti zot* 'in the integrity of my heart and the cleanness of my hands I have done this' (Gen 20:5), and [God's own] verifying him in that by His saying…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. masʾala. ² iʿtidhār (اعتذار) — "apology, [the] offering of excuse"; the legal/social act of presenting a justification for one's conduct.

content.hebrew: גם אנכי ידעתי כי בתם לבבך עשית זאת (בראשית כ:ו). אלגׄואב אן אבימלך קד אתי קביחא אסתחק לאגׄלה
content.english: …*gam anokhi yadaʿti ki ve-tom levavkha ʿasita zot* 'I too knew that in the integrity of your heart you have done this' (Gen 20:6). — The answer is that Abimelech committed an [act of] ugliness¹ on account of which he became deserving…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. qabīḥ.

content.hebrew: מא אנזל בה מן אלמצׄרה̈ והו אכׄדׄה לשרה כרהא עמ טׄנה [ב]קולהא ובקול א[ב]רהם אנהמא אכׄואן אדׄ ליס לה אכׄדׄ מרה̈ ליתזו[גׄ] בהא א[לא] ען רצׄא מנהא ומן אהלהא וליס תצדיקה פי ק[ול]ה בתם לבבי (בראשית כ:ה) מא יקתצׄי חסן דׄלך מן חיתׄ אנה לא יפיד אזיד מן אכׄדׄה להא עלי טׄנה אנהא אכׄת אברהם לא זוגׄתה ויקב[ח] אכׄדׄהא מע הדׄא אלטׄן. אלא תרי אנה צדקה פימא אדעא[ה] מן תמת לבב בדון מא אדאעה מן נקיון כפיו אלמפיד חסן א[לת]צרף פי אלאשיא כק׳ נקי כ[פים] (תהלים כד:ד) עלי אנה קד כאן מן [ח]קה לו אנצף נפסה אן לא יטׄן [בק]ולהמא אנהמא אכׄואן לכונהמא [פי] חכם אלמלגׄאיין אלי אכׄבארה בדׄלך למא קד אשתהר מן סירה̈ אלקום פי קתל [זו]גׄ אלמ[רה̈] ואכׄדׄהא פלו [כ]א[ן] צדיק נקי כפים עלי זעמה לכאן ינבגי לה [רפע] הדׄה אלסירה̈ מן בלדה ליאמן אלטארי אלי בלדה על נפסה אדׄא ורד אליה הו ומרתה פיכׄבר בדׄלך ען טמאנינה̈ ואן ורד רגׄל ואכׄתה ואכׄברא בכונהמא אכׄוין ורצׄיא במצאהרתה כאן דׄלך ה
content.english: …of what was sent down upon him of harm — namely, his taking of Sarah unwillingly¹ [on her part] in spite of his supposing, by her saying and by [A]braham's saying, that the two of them were brother [and sister]. For he [Abimelech] had no right to take a woman in marriage [ex]cept by her consent and the consent of her family. And His verifying him in his sa[yin]g *be-tom levavi* 'with integrity of heart' (Gen 20:5) does not require the goodness of [what he did], inasmuch as it conveys no more than his taking her on the supposition that she was Abraham's sister and not his wife — and [the act of] taking her remains ug[ly] even with this supposition. Do you not see that [God] verified him in what he claim[ed] of integrity-of-heart, but did not verify what he attributed to himself of *niqyon kappav* 'cleanness of hands' — which would convey the good[ness of] the [t]ransaction in the matter, as in [the verse] *neqi kap[payim]* 'clean of [hands]' (Ps 24:4). Even though, had he done his soul [the justice] of [self-]fairness, he should not have [su]pposed by their [the strangers'] [s]aying that they are brother and sister — for they were [in] the status of those forced² to declare such [a thing], given what was known of the custom of [his] people in killing the [hus]band of the wo[man] and taking her [for the king]. So, were he a *ṣaddiq neqi kappayim* on his own claim, it would have been incumbent upon him to [eradicate] this custom from his land — so that the stranger coming to his land may be secure as to himself when he arrives, he and his wife, and report that out of confidence; and if a man and his sister come and inform him that they are brother and sister and they are pleased to [enter] alliance with him, that would be [a fitting case]. End.
content.comments: ¹ karhan (كرهاً) — "unwillingly, [against her] will"; the legal term marking the absence of consent that constitutes a transgression. ² al-mulgaʾīn (الملجَئين) — "those forced, [those put] under duress"; the kalām legal category of duress, which suspends ordinary moral imputation.

content.hebrew: מסלה̈: אדׄא כאן קד צדקה פימא תברי ב[ה] מן הדׄא אלבאב פכיף י[ק]ול ואחשוך גם אנכי אותך מחטוא לי (בראשית כ:ו) ולא יצד [ע]ן אלכׄטא אלא מן הו מותׄר לה עאזם עליה.
content.english: [Another] questi[on]: if [God] had already verified him in what he was acquitting [him]self of in this respect, how can [He s]ay *va-eḥshokh gam anokhi otkha me-ḥaṭo li* 'and I too withheld you from sinning against me' (Gen 20:6) — for one is only kept back fr[o]m the sin if he is intending it and resolved upon it?

content.hebrew: אלגׄואב: אן קולה ואחשוך גם אנכי אותך מחטוא לי (בראשית כ:ו) עני בה כׄטא תׄאניא בעד אלאכׄר והו אלתקדם אליהא כקולה על כן לא נתתיך לנגוע אליה (בראשית כ:ו) ולא יפיד חסן מא תקדם מן אכׄדׄהא
content.english: The answer: that His saying *va-eḥshokh gam anokhi otkha me-ḥaṭo li* 'and I too withheld you from sinning against me' (Gen 20:6) means by it a second sin after the first — namely, the approaching of her, as in His saying *ʿal ken lo netattikha li-ngoaʿ eleha* 'therefore I did not let you touch her' (Gen 20:6). And it does not convey the goodness of what came before, of his taking her…

content.hebrew: למא סלף פיה ה
content.english: …for what is past in it. End.

content.hebrew: מסלה̈: כיף יחסן צדה ען אלקביח ואנזאל אלמצׄאר בה אלדׄי מעהא ילתגׄי אלי תרכה.
content.english: [Another] question: how is it good [for God] to withhold him from the ugly [act] and to send down upon him a harm by which he is [c]ompelled to leave it [off]?

content.hebrew: אלגׄואב: קד יחסן צד אלמכלף ען אלקביח אלדׄי יחאולה ב[א]ן יחאל....ובינה ולא יכון מכלפא באלאנצראף ענה טועא אדׄא לם יכן ללקדים גרץׄ פי תכליפה דׄלך ויכון מע דׄלך מכלפא בתכאליף אכׄר אדׄ ליס אסקאט תכליף ואחד ען אלמכלף יקת[צׄ]י אסקאט סאיר אלתכאליף [ענ]ה. אלא תרי אן אלשיךׄ אלפאני ק[ד] אסקט ענה תכליף תרך אלזנא והו מע דׄלך מכלף בתרך אלטׄל[ם ו]אלכדׄב וגירהמא ה
content.english: The answer: it is sometimes good [for God] to hold the morally accountable agent¹ back from the ugly [act] he is attempting, [b]y interpos[ing] [between him] and [the act]², so that he is no longer morally accountable for turning away from it voluntarily — when the Eternal has no specific purpose in his accountability for that. And he is, along with that, morally accountable for other obligations — for the dropping-away of one specific obligation from the accountable agent does not requi[r]e the dropping-away of the rest of the obligations [fro]m him. Do you not see that the extreme aged³ has [h]ad the obligation of refraining from fornication dropped away from him, while he is yet [bound by] the obligations of refraining from oppres[sion and] lying, and the rest. End.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. mukallaf. ² yuḥāl baynahu wa-baynahu (يُحال بينه وبينه) — "[the divine] interposition between him and [the act]"; the kalām category of God's blocking the conditions for an act, suspending the agent's effective obligation. ³ al-shaykh al-fānī (الشيخ الفاني) — "the extreme aged, [the one] worn-out [by old age]"; the legal category of the elderly in whom the relevant capacity has lapsed, with corresponding suspension of the relevant obligation.

content.hebrew: מסלה̈: אדׄא סל[ם א]ן אבימלך קד וקע מנה [ק]בח פי הדׄא אלבאב [פכ]יף יעאקב זוגׄתה וגׄואריה באלבלוי
content.english: [Another] questi[o]n: if it is [gra]nted that Abimelech committed an [u]gliness in this respect, [ho]w is it [good] to penalize his wife and his concubines with the affliction…

content.hebrew: אלתי [שפ]יוא מנהא ענד דעא אברהם פאן קיל למואפקתהם ראיה פי דׄלך ומעונתהם איאה כאן אלמעלום מן עאדה̈ נסא אלרגׄאל כראהה̈ דכׄול מרה̈ גירהן אליהם.
content.english: …of which they were [c]ured at Abraham's prayer? For if it be said: [it is] for their concurrence with his view in that and their aid to him — what is known from the custom of the wives of [such] men is rather their abhorrence of the entry of another woman to them.

content.hebrew: אלגׄואב: אנה אדׄא סל[ם] אנה לם יקע מן זוגׄה̈ אבימלך וגׄואריה קביח פי באב שרה [יכ]ון מא נזל בהן עקובה̈ [ע]ליה ואמכן כונה מחנה̈ עליהן בעוץׄ [ע]ליה ויכון אגתמאם אבימלך בהן ענד הדׄא אלמרץׄ ות[ב]לה עקובה̈ עליה כמות ולד אלפאסק ובעץׄ אעזאיה מן אלמכלפין ה
content.english: The answer: when it is [g]ranted that there occurred from the wife of Abimelech and his concubines no ugliness in the matter of Sarah, then what came down upon them is no penalty [u]pon them; and it is possible that it was a trial upon them, [with] [c]ompensation [u]pon him [for them]. And the cause of Abimelech's grieving over them at this illness and [c]alamity is a penalty upon him — like the death of the immoral one's child¹ and some of his loved ones from among the morally accountable. End.
content.comments: ¹ al-fāsiq (الفاسق) — "the immoral one, [the] transgressor"; the Muʿtazilite legal category of one who has committed a major sin without repenting. The analogy: just as the death of a fāsiq's child is experienced by the fāsiq as a penalty (the child's own death being a trial, not a penalty), so the illness of Abimelech's wives is a trial for them but a penalty for him.

content.hebrew: Gen 22:1
content.english: Gen 22:1

content.hebrew: ויהי אחר הדברים האלה והאלהים נסה –
content.english: **"And it was after these things, and God tested"** (*va-yehi aḥar ha-devarim ha-elleh ve-ha-Elohim nissah*). […]¹
content.comments: ¹ Lemma stands without commentary; the discussion picks up at nissah.

content.hebrew: – קולה נסה – קיל אמתחן מתׄל למען נסותך (דברים ח:טז) יעני צעב עליה אלתכליף אלדׄי ענדה טׄהרת טאעתה אלעטׄימה̈.
content.english: His saying **"tested"** (*nissah*). It is said: 'He tested [him]'¹, like *le-maʿan nassotekha* 'in order to test you' (Deut 8:16) — meaning, He made difficult for him the obligation² with which his great obedience would manifest.
content.comments: ¹ amtaḥana (امتحن) — "He tested, [subjected to] a trial"; the form-VIII verb of m-ḥ-n, the standard kalām term for divinely instigated testing, related to miḥna ("trial"; see Gen 18:25 footnote). ² See glossary s.v. taklīf.

content.hebrew: Gen 22:2
content.english: Gen 22:2

content.hebrew: אל ארץ המוריה – הו אעם מן קולה פי קצה̈ שלמה בה[ר] המוריה אשר נראה לדויד (דברי הימים ב׳ ג:א) פהר ה[מו]ריה הו אלגׄבל אלדׄי ענאה בקול אחד ההרים אשר אומר אליך (בראשית כב:ב) פכאן אלצקע מערוף בארץ המוריה לאגׄל אלגׄבל כמא יקול ען גׄמלה̈ ארץ ישראל על אדמת הקדש (זכריה ב:טז) וען גׄבל אלקדס [וה]שתחוו ליי בהר הקדש (ישעיהו כז:יג)
content.english: **"To the land of Moriah"** (*el erets ha-Moriyah*). It is more general than his saying in the story of Solomon, *be-h[ar] ha-Moriyah asher nirʾah le-David* 'on the moun[t] of Moriah which appeared to David' (2Chr 3:1). So *har ha-[Mo]riyah* is the mountain He meant by saying *aḥad he-harim asher omar elekha* 'one of the mountains which I shall tell you' (Gen 22:2). And the surrounding region was known as *erets ha-Moriyah* on account of the mountain — as he says of the entirety of the Land of Israel *ʿal admat ha-qodesh* 'on the holy soil' (Zech 2:16), and of the Mount of the Sanctuary *[ve-h]ishtaḥavu l-YY be-har ha-qodesh* 'and they shall prostrate to the LORD on the holy mountain' (Isa 27:13).

content.hebrew: – וקולה והעלהו שם לעלה – [א]לטׄאהר מנה אן י[פ]על פיה גׄמיע אלאפ[עאל] אלתי אדׄא פעל מתׄלהא פי אלחיואן סמי עליה ומן גׄמלתהא אלדׄבח ואלאחראק לאן לפטׄה̈ עלה אדׄא לם ירד בהא מא כאנת עליה פי אצל אללגה̈ מן מגׄרד צעו[ד] אלאנתׄ[י] בל מא א[נ]תקלת אליה פי א[לשר]ע פקד חצלת פאידתהא פיה אדׄן מא תקדם דׄכרה מן אלאפעאל אלת[י מ]ן גׄמלתהא אלדׄבח ואלאחראק והדׄה אלאפעאל [פ]י אל[על]ה לא תכׄתלף פי שער אברהם ולא פי שרע משה עליהמא אלסלם ואנמא אלמכׄתלף פיהא תרתיב אלאפעאל אדׄ פי שרע אברהם
content.english: And his saying **"and offer him up there as a burnt-offering"** (*ve-haʿalehu sham le-ʿolah*). The apparent sense of it is that he should [d]o to him all the ac[ts] which, when performed upon the animal, are named *ʿolah* — among them the slaughter (*dhabḥ*) and the burning (*iḥrāq*); for the term *ʿolah*, if it does not bring with it what it [originally] bore in the [un]derivative sense of the language, [namely] the mere ascen[ding] of the femal[e]¹ — but rather what [was] transferred to it in the [reli]gious [usage] — then its benefit [in this place] is realized thereby; [and] that includes what was mentioned earlier of the acts, [a]mong them the slaughter and the burning. And these acts [i]n the [ʿo]lah do not differ between the ritual law² of Abraham and the ritual law of Moses (peace be upon them both); rather, what differs in them is the order of the acts — for in the ritual law of Abraham…
content.comments: ¹ ṣuʿūd al-unthā (صعود الأنثى) — "the ascending of the female"; Ali appeals to a folk etymology of Hebrew ʿolah as derived from ʿ-l-h ("to go up") with the original sense of breeding ascent, then transferred in religious usage to the cultic act. ² sharʿ (شرع) — "ritual law, [religious] law-code"; the standard Qurʾānic/kalām term for revealed legal system, here applied across the Abrahamic and Mosaic covenants.

content.hebrew: דׄבח אלעלה עלי אלמדׄבח פי שרע משה וצׄע אלנאר עלי אלמדׄבח תׄם אלחטב תׄם צף אעצׄא אלשכׄץ אלמדׄבוח פי גיר אלמדׄבח [ע]לי אלחטב פקד אתפק אסמהא עלה פי שרעיהמא עליהמא אל[ס]לם ואכׄתלף תרתיב אלאפעאל אלמפעולה̈ פיהא. ואדׄא כאן אלדׄ[בח] ואלאחראק עלי אלוגׄהין לא בד מנה פי גׄמלה̈ אפעאל אלעלה וראינאה תעאלי קד נהאה עליה אלסלם ען אלדׄבח בעד חצול אלאפעאל מנה פי יצחק אלתי אכׄרהא ויקח את המאכלת לשחוט את בנו (בראשית כב:י) פלא בד מן תאויל דׄלך עלי וגׄה יטאבק דליל א[לע]קל אדׄ מא ידׄכרה
content.english: …the slaughter of the *ʿolah* is upon the altar; while in the ritual law of Moses, [the procedure is to] place the fire upon the altar, then the wood, then the arranging of the limbs of the slaughtered specimen — [the slaughtering itself being] outside the altar — [u]pon the wood. So its name *ʿolah* converges in their two ritual laws (peace be upon them both), but the order of acts performed in it diverges. And since the sl[aughter] and the burning are, on the two readings, indispensable in the totality of the acts of the *ʿolah* — and we see that [God] (may He be exalted) forbade him (peace be upon him) the slaughter after those acts had taken place on his part with Isaac, whose last is *va-yiqqaḥ et ha-maʾakhelet li-shḥot et beno* 'and he took the knife to slaughter his son' (Gen 22:10) — there is no escape from interpreting¹ that on a manner that conforms with the indication of [r]eason. For what some have said about that…
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. taʾwīl.

content.hebrew: בעצׄהם פי דׄלך מן אנה עז וגׄל אמרה באצעאדה [ע]לה [ו]כאן דׄלך באסתתׄני ולם ידׄכרה פי אלמוקף לא יסו[ג] למתׄל מא תקדם פי במא אדע כי אירשנה (בראשית טו:ח) מן אן כׄטאבה עז וגׄל דלאלה̈ עלי מראדה פלא יגׄוז אן יכון פי אמרה ונהיה אסתתׄני או שרט אלא וינטק בה מפ[רק]א בכׄטאבה ליפהם מראדה וא[לא] כׄרגׄ כׄטאבה מן כונה דלאלה̈ ו[א]סתדת אלטריק אלי מערפה̈ קצדה בכׄטאבה ואדׄא כאן כ[דׄ]לך פאלוגׄה פי תאויל הדׄא אלנץ אן יכון תעאלי למא קא[ל] לה והעלהו שם לעלה (בראשית כב:ב) קד [בי]ן לה מראדה בדׄלך באן [קאל ג]רצׄי בקולי לך עלה אן תאכׄדׄה ותכתפה ותצעדה עלי אלמדׄבח פוק אלחטב ותאכׄדׄ אלסכין מנתטׄרא מא אכלפך פיה בעד דׄלך. פקד פהם מראדה בקולה והעלהו שם לעלה (בראשית כב:ב) באלביאן אלמדׄכור וחצל אלנסיון עליה פי דׄלך מא טׄנה מן אנה סיומר פיה באלדׄ[ב]ח מא קדר מן קולה עז וגׄל כׄדׄ אלסכין בעד כתפ[ה] וגׄעלה עלי אלמדׄבח ואנתטׄר מא אכלפך פיה הו אמארה̈ תטׄננה א[ן] בעד דׄלך יקול לה אדׄבחה פתעטׄם עליה אלמחנה̈ בה כמא יטׄן מן י[ק]אל לה אצלח דואתך ואקלאמך וכׄדׄ אלדרגׄ בידך אנה סיומר בעד דׄלך באלכתאבה̈ ואדׄא אסתמר דׄלך פקד פהם אברהם מראדה סבחאנה בקולה והעלהו שם לעלה (בראשית כב:ב). ולם יכן פי דׄלך תאכׄיר ביאן בל אלביאן קד תקדם ענד אלאמר וחצל פי דׄלך מן אלאמתחאן אלקדר אלדׄי אראדה תעאלי פי תכליפה ה
content.english: …of theirs in this, [namely] that He (mighty and majestic) commanded him to offer him [u]p [as a] *ʿolah* [and] that this was under an unstated condition¹ [which] He did not mention at the [moment of] the command, is [n]ot ad[missible], in light of what was settled previously at *ba-mah edaʿ ki irashennah* (Gen 15:8) — that His (mighty and majestic) address is a [conventional] indication² of His meaning; so it is not admissible that in His command or prohibition there be an unstated condition or stipulation, unless He speak it [ex]pli[cit]ly in His address so that His intent be understood. Otherwise, His address departs from being an indication, [a]nd the road to knowledge of His [intended] aim by His address would be blocked. And since that is so, the manner [of interpretation] of this text is that He (may He be exalted), when He sa[id] to him *ve-haʿalehu sham le-ʿolah* 'and offer him up there as a burnt-offering' (Gen 22:2), had [explai]ned to him His meaning by that, [b]y [say]ing: 'my purpose by my saying to you *ʿolah* is that you take him, bind him, ascend him upon the altar above the wood, and take the knife — awaiting what I send you after that.' So he understood His meaning by His saying *ve-haʿalehu sham le-ʿolah* by the explanation mentioned. And the testing³ obtained upon him in this [is] what he supposed — that he would be commanded [further] with the slau[gh]ter — [a supposition] warranted by his [God's] (mighty and majestic) saying 'take the knife after binding [him] and placing him on the altar, and await what I send you after that' is an indicator⁴ producing in him the supposition that afterward [God] would say to him 'slaughter him,' so that the trial would press upon him by that — as one [thinks] when it is [s]aid to him 'prepare your inkwell and your pens and take the scroll in your hand,' that he is going to be commanded after that with the writing. And since this continued, Abraham had [already] understood His intent (praise be to Him) by His saying *ve-haʿalehu sham le-ʿolah* (Gen 22:2). And there was in this no delaying of clarification⁵; rather, the clarification was given at the command, and the testing in it produced the measure He (may He be exalted) intended in his moral accountability. End.
content.comments: ¹ See glossary s.v. istithnāʾ. ² See glossary s.v. dalāla. ³ al-nisyān (النسيان) — read here as al-niṣyān / al-naṣīʿ; Ali uses the cognate of the Hebrew nissah, rendered consistently as "testing" or "trial." ⁴ See glossary s.v. amāra. ⁵ See glossary s.v. taʾkhīr al-bayān.

content.hebrew: וקד קיל פי דׄלך וגׄה אכׄר והו אנה אדׄא כון אלא[מ]ר עלי [א]לתראכׄי לא עלי אלפור וכאן קד מצׄי עלי אברהם
content.english: And another manner has been said in this — namely, that if the co[m]mand were on [the standard of] postponable¹ [execution] rather than immediate², and [in fact] had passed upon Abraham…
